facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]: $\mathbb R^n$ is the function space on $n$ with its coordinatewise real vector-space operations.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[def-linear-map]]: a map $T:V\to W$ between real vector spaces is linear when $T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v)$ for all real $a,b$ and vectors $u,v$.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]: for $n\ge1$, $d_1(x,z)=\sum_{k<n}|x_k-z_k|$ is a metric on $\mathbb R^n$.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[def-ip-forward-map-and-solution-classes]]: the solution-class target is a metric space $(Q,d_Q)$ with map $q:U\to Q$; the identity target is allowed.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[def-ip-identifiability-and-stability-modulus]]: identifiability is equal data implying equal target classes, and a uniform stability modulus bounds target-class distance as a function of data distance.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[thm-ip-kernel-directions-preclude-unrestricted-recovery]]: if one datum lies within radius $\delta$ of both forward data, every estimator's maximum target-class loss is at least half the target-class distance.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[lem-square-summable-sequences-form-a-hilbert-space]]: $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ consists of sequences with finite sum of squares, uses its canonical inner-product norm, and is a real Hilbert space.

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]: for a nonnegative family, its sum is the supremum of its finite subsums.

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]: $e_n$ is the family that is $1$ at coordinate $n$ and $0$ elsewhere.

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] [[def-hilbert-space]]: a real Hilbert space is a real inner-product space complete for its induced norm metric.

facts.label: F11
facts.text: [F11] [[lem-geometric-sequence-null]]: if $|r|<1$ then $r^n\to0$, and if $|r|>1$ then $|r|^n$ diverges to $+\infty$.

facts.label: F12
facts.text: [F12] [[lem-power-monotone]]: for $a>0$ all natural powers $a^n$ are positive, and for $0\le a\le1$ they satisfy $a^n\le1$.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is the hypothesis of the compact norm-limit theorem, Hilbert adjoint, and compact square-root results used below.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]] and [[lem-square-summable-sequences-form-a-hilbert-space]]: $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ has norm squared $\sum_j|x_j|^2$, unit coordinate vectors $e_j$, and is a complete real Hilbert space.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]] and [[def-operator-norm]]: The inner product satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz and the operator norm is the supremum of $\|Tx\|$ over $\|x\|\le1$.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]], and [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]: Every bounded operator on a Hilbert space has a unique adjoint satisfying $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,T^*y\rangle$; self-adjointness is $T^*=T$, and positivity is $\langle Tx,x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x$.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]] and [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]]: Bounded finite-rank maps are compact, and a norm limit of compact maps into a Banach space is compact under Countable Choice.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[lem-positive-square-root-of-a-compact-positive-operator]] and [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]: The positive square root of a compact positive operator is unique and acts on an eigenvector of eigenvalue $\lambda$ by $\sqrt{\lambda}$; compact spectral multipliers act eigenvalue by eigenvalue.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[def-ip-index-source-ball]] and [[def-ip-power-source-set]]: The source ball is the image of the radius-$\rho$ vector ball under its spectral index multiplier; the power index is $t^\nu$, and the logarithmic candidate defines a source ball once it is bounded on the compact spectrum.

facts.label: F7
F8
facts.text: [F8] [[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]], [[def-real-power]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]], [[thm-real-power-laws]], [[cor-archimedean-reciprocal]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]], and [[def-complete-ordered-real-field]]: The real field is complete and ordered; $\log 1=0$, $\exp(0)=1$, and positive-base real powers are positive. [F4] [[lem-taylor-lagrange-remainder-from-mean-value]]: for a $C^3$ function
with third derivative bounded by $C$, expansion through degree two at

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A positive trace-class operator is compact; its positive square root exists under Countable Choice and is Hilbert–Schmidt with squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm equal to the trace. [[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-positive-square-root-of-a-compact-positive-operator]], [[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]], [[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]], [[thm-trace-of-a-positive-operator-is-the-sum-of-its-eigenvalues]], [[lem-compositions-with-a-compact-operator-are-compact]]

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Under the Axiom of Choice, finite jointly Gaussian blocks with zero cross-covariance are independent. facts.label: F7

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] Tonelli interchanges expectation and a countable sum of nonnegative random variables; composing a Hilbert–Schmidt operator with a bounded one preserves the Hilbert–Schmidt property, and a product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators is trace class. [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-hilbert-schmidt-operators-form-a-two-sided-ideal]], [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]]

facts.label: F9

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] For each fixed $u\in D$, $y\mapsto\tfrac12(y-u)^2$ is a continuous real polynomial; the open slices $\{u\}\times\mathbb R$ show that $\Phi$ is jointly continuous. Every open $O\subseteq D\times\mathbb R$ is $\bigcup_{u\in D}\{u\}\times O_u$ with each $O_u$ open in $\mathbb R$, and each such rectangle belongs to the product sigma-algebra. facts.label: F3

facts.label: F4

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Every singleton of the real line is closed, so every subset of the finite set $D$ is Borel; consequently every function from $D$ to a measurable target, including the explicitly defined potentials, is measurable. [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]

[A1] AC is assumed by the repository's multivariate-normal, Gaussian-process,

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] A finite Gaussian law is characterized by its Gaussian scalar
projections, permits singular covariance, and has the covariance-square-root
representation. [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The prior is supported on $m_0+\operatorname{Ran}(C_0)$ and admits
coordinates $C_0=U\Lambda U^T$ with a standard Gaussian vector on that range.
[[lem-ip-singular-gaussian-support-and-pseudoinverse]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] A real process is Gaussian when all its finite linear combinations are
normal. [[def-gaussian-process]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] Independence of random elements is independence of their generated
sigma-algebras. [[def-independent-random-elements]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] Measurable functions of independent random elements remain independent.
[[lem-measurable-functions-preserve-independence]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] For a finite Gaussian process with independent Gaussian observation noise,
if the observed covariance is positive definite, the conditional law of the
test vector is the Gaussian with mean
$m_*+K_{*X}(K_{XX}+R)^{-1}(y-m_X)$ and covariance
$K_{**}-K_{*X}(K_{XX}+R)^{-1}K_{X*}$, defined for every $y$ even when the
prior or conditional covariance is singular.
[[thm-finite-gaussian-process-posterior-and-predictive-laws]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] A positive-definite Gaussian observation-noise covariance has the
Lebesgue density proportional to
$\exp(-\tfrac12 z^T\Gamma^{-1}z)$, which is strictly positive everywhere.
[[thm-nondegenerate-multivariate-normal-law-has-density]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text:
[F8] The inverse-problem potential update is the prior reweighted by
$e^{-\Phi_y}$ and normalized by its evidence when that evidence is positive
and finite. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

facts.label: F9
facts.text:
[F9] A finite continuous potential with lower envelope $0$ under a proper
prior on a separable Banach space has positive finite evidence at every datum.
[[thm-ip-function-space-posterior-propriety]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] AC is assumed by the Cameron–Martin and support interfaces below. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

facts.label: A2
facts.text: [A2] HB and countable choice are assumed for the norming-family interface used to justify symmetry on the centered ball. [[def-hahn-banach-extension-principle-relative]], [[def-countable-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] $W$ is Borel measurable, and every $\ell\in B^*$ applied to $W$ is a centered real normal variable. [[def-borel-gaussian-random-element-on-a-separable-banach-space]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The Cameron–Martin space is the completion of the covariance quotient, its canonical injection is continuous and injective, and the range of the covariance quotient is dense in $E$. [[def-banach-gaussian-covariance-operator-and-rkhs]], [[thm-banach-gaussian-covariance-rkhs-is-well-defined]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] For each $h\in E$, the law of $W+ih$ has density $\exp(z_h-\|h\|_E^2/2)$ with respect to $\mu$, where $h\mapsto z_h\in L^2(\mu)$ is linear and isometric, $z_h$ is centered normal with variance $\|h\|_E^2$, and $z_{C\ell}=\ell(W)$ almost surely. Since the covariance range is dense in $E$, this also makes $z_h$ an $L^2$ limit of continuous-linear Gaussian coordinates. [[thm-cameron-martin-translation-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law]], [[def-multivariate-normal-law]], [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A separable Banach space is Polish, every Borel probability on a Polish space is tight, and the support of a centered tight Borel Gaussian is $\overline{iE}$ in $B$. Thus $0$ belongs to the support and every open ball about $0$ has positive $\mu$-mass. [[def-polish-space]], [[thm-every-borel-probability-on-a-polish-space-is-tight]], [[thm-support-of-banach-gaussian-is-closure-of-rkhs]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For every $h\in E$ and $r>0$, $\mu(\overline B_B(ih,r))\le\mu(\overline B_B(0,r))$. [[lem-ip-banach-gaussian-cm-shift-ball-bound]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] A real separable Banach space has a countable family $(\ell_j)$ with $\|x\|_B=\sup_j|\ell_j(x)|$. [[lem-separable-banach-has-countable-norming-family]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The Axiom of Choice states that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

facts.label: A2
facts.text: [A2] Countable Choice supplies a choice function for every countable family of nonempty sets; this is the branch assumed by the compact-SVD coordinate model. [[def-countable-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The Gaussian sequence inverse model has parameter $\theta\in\ell^2$, product-Borel data $Z\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$, and coordinates $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j$ with independent standard normal $\xi_j$. Multiplying by $s_j>0$ gives $Y_j=s_j\theta_j+\epsilon\xi_j$. [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] In a finite linear Gaussian model with Gaussian prior covariance $C_0$ and positive-definite observation-noise covariance $\Gamma$, the posterior covariance is $C_0-C_0A^T(AC_0A^T+\Gamma)^{-1}AC_0$ and the posterior mean is $m_0+C_0A^T(AC_0A^T+\Gamma)^{-1}(y-Am_0)$. [[thm-ip-finite-linear-gaussian-posterior]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Under AC, a consistent family of finite Gaussian laws on countably many real coordinates has a unique probability law on the product cylinder sigma-algebra. [[thm-gaussian-process-exists-from-mean-and-positive-semidefinite-covariance-kernel]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Independence of random elements is independence of their generated sigma-algebras; the assumed independent prior and noise coordinates give independent coordinate pairs. [[def-independent-random-elements]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Finite measures that agree on a generating $\pi$-system and on the whole space agree on its generated sigma-algebra. [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] A $\pi$-system contained in a Dynkin system has its generated sigma-algebra contained in that Dynkin system. [[thm-dynkin-pi-lambda]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Increasing nonnegative measurable functions satisfy convergence of their integrals to the integral of their pointwise limit. [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] For a nonnegative measurable function $f$ and $t>0$, $\mu\{f\ge t\}\le t^{-1}\int f\,d\mu$. [[thm-chebyshev-markov-inequality-for-the-integral]]

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] A posterior contraction rate is defined by the expected fixed-truth posterior tail condition in the Statement. [[def-ip-posterior-contraction-rate]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The posterior coordinate mean and variance are $\lambda_jY_j/s_j$ and $v_j$, and the expected posterior squared error is the displayed nonnegative sum; posterior tail mass is bounded by that sum divided by the squared radius. [[thm-ip-conjugate-gaussian-sequence-contraction]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A rate is established when expected posterior mass outside every diverging multiple tends to zero under the fixed-truth law. [[def-ip-posterior-contraction-rate]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The Gaussian sequence inverse model has $\theta^\dagger\in\ell^2$, positive singular values, product-Borel observations, and independent standard-normal noise coordinates. [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] For positive bases, real powers satisfy $a^x=\exp(x\log a)$ and the ordinary exponent laws. [[def-real-power]], [[thm-real-power-laws]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For every $q>0$, the geometric series $\sum_{k\ge0}2^{-2qk}$ converges and equals $(1-2^{-2q})^{-1}$. [[thm-geometric-series]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The standard coordinate basis makes $H=\ell^2$ a separable real Hilbert space. For the diagonal covariance, positivity and self-adjointness follow from $\langle\Gamma x,x\rangle=\sum_j\tau_j^2x_j^2\ge0$ and $\langle\Gamma x,y\rangle=\langle x,\Gamma y\rangle$. Finite-rank truncations converge in operator norm, so $\Gamma$ is compact; its diagonal rank-one expansion has nuclear sum $\sum_j\tau_j^2<\infty$, so it is trace class. [[thm-hilbert-space-with-a-given-orthonormal-basis-is-ell-two-of-the-index-set]], [[def-separable-space]], [[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]], [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]], [[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] A positive self-adjoint trace-class covariance on a separable real Hilbert space defines a Borel centered Hilbert-valued Gaussian random element with that covariance. [[lem-positive-trace-class-covariance-defines-hilbert-gaussian]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] A finite vector is multivariate normal when all its linear projections are normal. [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] Finite jointly Gaussian blocks with zero cross-covariance are independent, including for singular covariance matrices. [[lem-uncorrelated-jointly-gaussian-blocks-are-independent]]

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] The notation $N(m,\sigma^2)$ denotes the law of a normal variable with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$. [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]

facts.label: F5

[[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] Composing a measurable function with a Borel scalar function preserves
measurability; the real exponential is continuous, and finite arithmetic and
lattice operations preserve measurability.
[[thm-composition-with-borel-functions-preserves-measurability]] [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] [[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]]

$\xi\sim\mu_0$. [[alg-ip-prior-preserving-crank-nicolson]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] A separable Hilbert space has a finite or countable complete orthonormal
basis. The product of two at most countable sets is at most countable.
[[def-separable-space]] [[lem-countable-iff-surjection-from-n]] [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] [[thm-product-of-countable]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] $H^*$ denotes the continuous dual, and every continuous linear functional
of a centered Borel Gaussian random element has a centered real normal law.
[[def-dual-space-of-a-normed-space]] [[def-borel-gaussian-random-element-on-a-separable-banach-space]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] A centered Borel Gaussian random element in a separable Banach space has
finite moments of every polynomial order by Fernique exponential-square
integrability. [[thm-fernique-integrability-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] Independent random elements have the product of their marginal laws as
their joint law. Independence is independence of the sigma-algebras generated
by the random elements. [[def-independent-random-elements]] [[thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] For independent scalar normal variables, the characteristic function of
a finite linear combination is the product of the scalar normal
characteristic functions; uniqueness of characteristic functions then makes
the combination normal, including when its variance is zero.
[[lem-characteristic-functions-under-affine-maps-and-independent-sums]] [[lem-characteristic-function-of-a-normal-law]] [[thm-uniqueness-of-a-law-from-its-characteristic-function]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] A finite-dimensional normal law is determined by its mean and covariance,
including in the singular case. [[def-multivariate-normal-law]] [[lem-characteristic-function-of-a-multivariate-normal-law]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text:
[F8] Under AC's consequence Countable Choice, two Borel probabilities on a
separable Hilbert space with the same finite coordinate laws in a complete
orthonormal basis are equal. [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] [[lem-ip-separable-hilbert-borel-laws-determined-by-orthonormal-coordinates]]

facts.label: F9
facts.text:
[F9] For independent integrable real random variables, expectations of their
products factor; covariance is the expectation of the product of centered
variables, and expectation is linear on integrable functions.
[[thm-factorization-of-expectations-for-independent-variables]] [[def-moments-variance-and-covariance]] [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]

facts.label: F10
facts.text:
[F10] For second-countable spaces, the Borel sigma-algebra on the product
equals the product sigma-algebra, which is generated by measurable rectangles.
[[def-second-countable-space]] [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]] [[lem-borel-product-of-second-countable-spaces]] [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]

facts.text: [F2] A prior on a full-mass Borel forward domain and a finite continuous potential with a common integrable lower envelope have positive finite evidence and a normalized posterior. facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] If a nonnegative measurable function has integral zero, it vanishes almost everywhere; integrating on a measurable set is integrating its indicator times the function. [[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]] [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] The proposal rule $Q_\beta$ and accept-reject rule $P_\beta$ are Borel probability kernels; for each $u$,
$$Q_\beta(u,B)=\int_H\mathbf1_B(\rho u+\beta z)\,\mu_0(dz),\qquad P_\beta(u,A)=\int_A\alpha(u,v)Q_\beta(u,dv)+\mathbf1_A(u)(1-a(u)),$$
where $a(u)=\int_H\alpha(u,v)Q_\beta(u,dv)$. [[lem-ip-pcn-transition-kernel-is-measurable]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] If $w(u)=e^{-\bar\Phi(u)}$, then $\mu(du)=Z^{-1}w(u)\mu_0(du)$, $w(u)=0$ when $\bar\Phi(u)=+\infty$, and $\alpha(u,v)=0$ if either potential is infinite. [[alg-ip-prior-preserving-crank-nicolson]] [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] For $U_0,\xi$ independent with law $\mu_0$ and $V_0=\rho U_0+\beta\xi$, the joint Borel law of $(U_0,V_0)$ is symmetric under coordinate swap; on the separable Hilbert product, the Borel sigma-algebra equals the product sigma-algebra. [[lem-ip-pcn-reference-pair-law-is-symmetric]] [[lem-borel-product-of-second-countable-spaces]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A prior and probability kernel define a joint flow probability measure with the rectangle formula and nonnegative iterated-integral identity. [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]] [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]] [[def-probability-measure]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Equality of probability laws is preserved under measurable changes of variables, and integration against a law equals expectation of the corresponding random-element function. [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] [[thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The product of two probability measures exists and has the rectangle formula; the rectangle criterion then makes its coordinate projections independent random elements. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]] [[thm-rectangle-criterion-for-independent-random-elements]] [[def-independent-random-elements]] [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] A probability kernel is reversible with respect to a probability measure when its joint flow equals its coordinate transpose; this definition requires no density. [[def-general-state-reversibility-by-symmetric-flow-measure]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] Reversibility with respect to a probability measure implies its invariance. [[thm-general-state-reversibility-implies-invariance]]

Its coordinates are $2^{-j/2}X_j$. [[lem-ip-gaussian-series-prior-regularity]] [[lem-ip-coordinate-vectors-form-a-basis-of-ell-two]]

facts.text: [F5] A $N(0,1)$ variable has mean zero, second moment one, and fourth moment three. [[lem-normal-location-scale-mean-and-variance]] [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]

facts.label: F6

facts.label: F9

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] The Borel sigma-algebra of a topological space is generated by its open sets; Borel measurable functions are closed under finite arithmetic operations. [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]] [[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]]

facts.label: F11
facts.text: [F11] The Borel sigma-algebra on a product of second-countable spaces is the product sigma-algebra, and integrating a nonnegative product-measurable function against a probability kernel gives a measurable function of its source point. [[lem-borel-product-of-second-countable-spaces]] [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]] [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]

facts.label: F12

facts.label: F13

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A measurable function with finite integral of its absolute value represents an $L^1$ function; here $\ell\in L^1[a,b]$. [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The indefinite integral of an $L^1$ function is absolutely continuous. [[cor-the-indefinite-integral-of-an-l-one-function-is-absolutely-continuous]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Under [A1], every absolutely continuous function is the integral of its almost-everywhere derivative, and that derivative is integrable. [[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-absolutely-continuous-functions]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] If an absolutely continuous function is followed by a Lipschitz function on its image, the composition is absolutely continuous. [[thm-a-lipschitz-function-after-an-absolutely-continuous-function-is-absolutely-continuous]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The product of absolutely continuous functions is absolutely continuous. [[lem-the-product-of-two-absolutely-continuous-functions-is-absolutely-continuous]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The exponential has derivative $e^r$; the mean-value theorem therefore makes $r\mapsto e^{-r}$ Lipschitz on every compact interval. [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[lem-mean-value-theorem-on-closed-interval]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] At a point where the inner and outer derivatives exist, the ordinary chain rule gives the derivative of their composition; the product rule gives the derivative of a product. [[thm-chain-rule]], [[lem-derivative-algebra-and-chain-rules]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] When $a<b$, reflection on $(a,b)$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism, so substitution preserves Lebesgue integrals of $L^1$ functions; the endpoints have measure zero. [[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are available. They are used through the integrable-coefficient Grönwall estimate and the C$^1$ change-of-variables theorem. [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[lem-ip-gronwall-with-integrable-coefficient]], [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The space $C(J,\mathbb R^d)$ with the supremum norm is complete on every compact interval $J$. [[lem-vector-valued-continuous-curve-space-is-complete]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Every contraction of a nonempty complete metric space has a unique fixed point, obtained by iterating from any initial point. [[thm-banach-fixed-point]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The norm of a vector-valued integral is bounded by the integral of the norm. [[thm-norm-inequality-for-the-vector-valued-integral]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The indefinite integral of an integrable scalar function is continuous and absolutely continuous; integrals of nonnegative functions are nonnegative and monotone. [[cor-the-indefinite-integral-of-an-l-one-function-is-absolutely-continuous]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The integral of a continuous Banach-valued curve is differentiable with derivative equal to the integrand. [[lem-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-banach-valued-continuous-curves]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] A continuous real function on a compact metric space is uniformly continuous. [[thm-heine-cantor-metric]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] For a continuous vector field that is $C^1$ in the state variable, when solutions through nearby initial states exist on a common compact time interval, the solution is $C^1$ in initial state and its derivative solves the variational equation. [[thm-c1-dependence-of-solutions-on-initial-data]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] The chain rule for total derivatives gives the derivative of a composition of $C^1$ Euclidean maps. [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] The determinant differential and Jacobi formula give $D\det(A)[H]=\det(A)\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}H)$ for invertible $A$; trace is cyclic. [[thm-determinant-differential-and-jacobis-formula]], [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]], [[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]], [[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] A C$^1$ diffeomorphism of open Euclidean sets satisfies the change-of-variables formula for every nonnegative Lebesgue-measurable integrand under Countable Choice. [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]

facts.label: F11
facts.text: [F11] The scalar chain and product rules, exponential derivative, and mean-value theorem justify the integrating-factor identity and show that a differentiable function with zero derivative on an interval is constant. [[thm-chain-rule]], [[lem-derivative-algebra-and-chain-rules]], [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[lem-mean-value-theorem-on-closed-interval]]

facts.label: F12
facts.text: [F12] $L^1([0,T])$ consists of measurable functions whose absolute values have finite Lebesgue integral. [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]

facts.label: F13
facts.text: [F13] Joint continuity is continuity for the product Euclidean topology and is preserved by composition with a continuous curve. [[def-continuous-map-top]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice for standard-Borel disintegration existence and simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces with their Borel sigma-algebras are standard Borel. [[lem-finite-euclidean-space-is-standard-borel]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For a probability measure on a product of standard-Borel spaces, a probability-kernel disintegration satisfies the rectangle identity and is unique outside one common marginal-null set. The theorem also gives the corresponding iterated-integral identity for nonnegative product-measurable functions. [[thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A probability kernel has a probability-measure section at every parameter, and each fixed-set evaluation is measurable in the parameter. [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Borel coordinate maps and finite coordinate permutations are measurable for the relevant finite-product Borel sigma-algebras, which agree with the product sigma-algebras. [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]], [[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]], [[lem-coordinate-maps-and-permutations-are-measurable-on-finite-products]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Integrating a nonnegative product-measurable function against a probability kernel gives a measurable function of the parameter. [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The product of probability measures has the rectangle formula, and Tonelli identifies its nonnegative integral with either iterated integral. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the stated ODE hypotheses give a jointly continuous triangular terminal flow with bijective fibers; the optional C$^1$ density clause is separate. [[lem-ip-lipschitz-ode-triangular-flow-and-c1-density]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] In a proper Bayesian model on standard-Borel parameter and data spaces, the data-indexed conditional posterior kernel is a version of the posterior and is unique as a probability measure outside one data-marginal-null set. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

references.title: Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed.
references.locator: Regular conditional distributions and disintegration for standard Borel variables; the local proof supplies the rectangle identity and common-null-set uniqueness interfaces used here.

references.title: S. R. S. Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4
references.locator: Conditional distributions, disintegration and conditional integration for standard Borel spaces.

The pushforward and Tonelli calculations are choice-free once the kernels are supplied. The ODE flow supplier uses only Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, both consequences of AC.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] AC is assumed for the conditional-expectation projection and standard-Borel posterior-kernel interfaces. Its implications include Countable Choice and Dependent Choice for the flow lemma. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[thm-conditional-expectation-is-the-l2-orthogonal-projection]], [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] In a proper Bayesian model, $\pi$ is the joint unknown/data law and $\pi_y$ is a version of the posterior conditional law; values on a $\pi_Y$-null set are not fixed by the conditional identity. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]], [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For a square-integrable target, the conditional expectation given $\sigma(t,X_t,Y)$ is the unique $L^2$ minimizer of the population squared prediction loss, coordinatewise. [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]], [[thm-conditional-expectation-is-the-l2-orthogonal-projection]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Under AC, a conditional expectation given a random element in a standard Borel space has a measurable representative as a function of that conditioning element; the identity with the conditional expectation holds almost surely. [[cor-conditional-expectation-as-a-measurable-function-of-the-conditioning-variable]], [[lem-finite-euclidean-space-is-standard-borel]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Independent sampling from $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$, $\eta$, and $\pi$ gives the stated product training law; product probabilities have the rectangle formula, and the expectation of a finite sum of integrable losses is the sum of their expectations. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] A fitted field satisfying the integrable spatial-Lipschitz and origin-growth assumptions has a unique global flow and a continuous terminal map; these facts do not certify that its output law is the target. [[lem-ip-lipschitz-ode-triangular-flow-and-c1-density]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] If the exact triangular terminal map has joint pushforward $\pi$, its exact conditional fibers push $\eta$ to $\pi_y$ for $\pi_Y$-almost every datum; this needs the joint identity as a separate hypothesis. [[thm-ip-exact-triangular-transport-disintegrates-to-posterior]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] The six-term posterior-computation budget is a telescoping ledger and supplies no learned-flow regression or optimizer bound. [[def-ip-posterior-computation-error-budget]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Blechschmidt et al. specify that conditional flow matching trains from prior-predictive joint samples and reference draws using a conditional velocity regression objective without evaluating the likelihood. facts.text: [F2] The density-based independent-MH correction requires the unnormalized target posterior density in its target/proposal ratio. [[lem-metropolis-hastings-density-ratio]], [Owen, Chapter 11 §11.4](https://artowen.su.domains/mc/Ch-MCMC.pdf)

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Under the stated dominated model, the unnormalized posterior density is prior density times likelihood; evidence normalization does not remove the likelihood from an MH ratio. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The C$^1$ flow clause can supply a proposal density by the Jacobian formula, independently of whether the likelihood density is available. [[lem-ip-lipschitz-ode-triangular-flow-and-c1-density]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] If a distinct exact triangular map satisfies the joint pushforward identity, conditional transport can yield the posterior without evaluating that density; the identity is a separate exactness hypothesis. [[thm-ip-exact-triangular-transport-disintegrates-to-posterior]]

references.title: Jan Blechschmidt, Oliver G. Ernst, Moritz Poguntke, and Björn Sprungk, Flow Matching for Fast Posterior Sampling in Bayesian Inverse Problems

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 11 §11.4
references.locator: Independent Metropolis–Hastings accepts by the target-to-proposal density ratio, which requires an evaluable unnormalized target density when used for a correction.

facts.text: [A1] The ultrafilter lemma says every filter on a set extends to an ultrafilter ([[def-ultrafilter-extension-principle]]).

facts.label: A2
facts.text: [A2] Dependent choice supplies an infinite sequence following any everywhere-extendible relation ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

facts.label: A3
facts.text: [A3] HB is the real dominated-extension principle for linear functionals ([[def-hahn-banach-extension-principle-relative]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] DC implies countable choice, the principle that every countable family of nonempty sets admits a choice function ([[lem-dependent-choice-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Under countable choice, every complete real inner-product space is reflexive ([[thm-hilbert-spaces-are-reflexive-by-riesz-representation]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Under the ultrafilter lemma, DC, and HB, every bounded sequence in a real reflexive Banach space has a weakly convergent subsequence ([[lem-bounded-minimising-sequence-has-a-weakly-convergent-subsequence]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Under HB, weak convergence implies lower semicontinuity of the norm ([[cor-weak-convergence-implies-lower-semicontinuity-of-the-norm]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Every nonempty real set bounded below has an infimum, and if $m=\inf S$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ some $s\in S$ satisfies $s<m+\varepsilon$ ([[def-infimum]], [[thm-infimum-property]], [[lem-inf-epsilon]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The objective is the finite nonnegative sum $J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x)=\frac12\|F(x)-y\|_Y^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-x_0\|_X^2$ on $D$ ([[def-ip-nonlinear-tikhonov-functional]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Sequential graph closure identifies a joint weak limit: if $x_n\in D$, $x_n\rightharpoonup x$, and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$, then $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$ ([[def-ip-weakly-closed-nonlinear-forward-map]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is assumed. No stronger form of choice is assumed.

facts.label: A2
facts.text: [A2] The data satisfy $y=F(x^\dagger)$ and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$.

facts.label: A3
facts.text: [A3] The closed outer ball lies in $U$, $x^\dagger$ is within distance $r$ of $x_0$, $F'$ is continuous in operator norm on $U$, and the derivative bound and uniform two-point tangential-cone inequality in the Statement hold on that ball.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[alg-ip-nonlinear-landweber-discrepancy]]: the iteration is $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta))$ and the discrepancy check is made before the finite-budget check.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[def-ip-tangential-cone-condition]]: at a base point $x$, the local TCC bounds $\|F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x)h\|_Y$ by $\eta\|F(x+h)-F(x)\|_Y$. The theorem assumes this exact orientation uniformly for pairs in the outer ball.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]] and [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]]: $\langle Au,v\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*v\rangle_X$ and $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ for every bounded Hilbert-space operator $A$.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]: the real inner product is symmetric and $\|u\|_X^2=\langle u,u\rangle_X$; the corresponding expansion is $\|u+v\|_X^2=\|u\|_X^2+2\langle u,v\rangle_X+\|v\|_X^2$.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]: $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\,\|v\|$.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]: $\|u+v\|\le\|u\|+\|v\|$ in each real Hilbert space.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[def-hilbert-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $X$ for the induced norm converges in $X$.

facts.label: F8

external_boundary.declared_source_remarks:
Kaltenbacher's 2024 paper treats the three-dimensional unit ball with background conductivity $\sigma_{\rm bg}\equiv1$, quadratic penalty $\check R(\sigma)=\frac12\|\sigma\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}^2$, $s_1\in(5/2,7/2)$, and truth $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ for $s_2\in(s_1,2s_1-1)$. Its Theorem 10 reports a logarithmic VSC exponent

$$\nu_{\rm paper}:=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_1-1},$$

with $b=3/4$, and Corollary 11 reports a conductivity-norm rate using that exponent divided by the source parameter $\widetilde p$ for the joint, split, and frozen-Newton methods. These printed formulas are source assertions; the locally proved EIT conclusions use the corrected exponent and parameter qualifications below.

The cited Weidling Theorem 6.15 at $p=2$ gives denominator $s_2-1$ in the corresponding logarithmic exponent. In addition, the quadratic Bregman distance is one half the squared $H^{s_1}$ norm error, so a Bregman rate with logarithmic exponent $\nu$ yields a norm exponent $\nu/2$; this abstract implication alone does not supply every exponent reported by Corollary 11. The sufficient parameter coupling in the abstract rate theorem requires $\alpha H(c/\alpha)\asymp\delta^2$ for a fixed $c>0$. For a logarithmic index with $H(q)\asymp(\log q)^{-\nu}$, no pure-power choice $\alpha\asymp\delta^{\widetilde p}$ with $0<\widetilde p\le2$ satisfies this two-sided coupling. Kaltenbacher's Remark 1 separately asserts that pure powers still give the same logarithmic rate; that separate assertion needs an independent derivation and is not ruled out solely by failure of the sufficient coupling. The local joint and frozen EIT theorems assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, use the corrected exponent $\nu=(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)/(s_2-1)$, retain the entire stated Sobolev/Besov truth range, and prove the conductivity norm exponent $\nu/2$. They give balanced parameters, every strict pure power $0<\widetilde p<2$, and the nominal endpoint $\widetilde p=2$ with an explicit stronger actual-noise condition. The universal abstract endpoint assertion under arbitrary deterministic noise bounded only by $\delta$ is false, as shown by the exact quadratic counterexample in the endpoint lemma; that example does not claim to be an EIT-specific counterexample.

The local application uses mean-zero Neumann currents and boundary-mean-zero Neumann states. Its data space is the centered sequence $(\mathscr N_\sigma-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k}$ in $\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$, or equivalently the corresponding affine translate for absolute voltages. This centering is necessary: at the background conductivity $1$, the uncentered voltage columns have norms $1/\ell$ with multiplicity $2\ell+1$, so their squared sum diverges. The centered Neumann-map differentiability, sharp $H^1$ logarithmic stability, exact intrinsic Sobolev/Besov source inequality, augmented factorization and inverse, frozen Taylor estimate, and regularizer/penalty compatibility now have local proofs. The sharp stability proof retains the Fourier modulation in the CGO remainder and integrates its negative-Sobolev norm before absorption; it does not use the invalid unmodulated pointwise inference in the printed Weidling proof.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable Choice supplies the countable diagonal selections in the compactness and weak-subsequence arguments. ([[def-countable-choice]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate]]: $Au^\dagger=f$, $R(u^\dagger)$ is minimal over exact solutions, and $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$; the Hilbert adjoint satisfies $\langle Au,p\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*p\rangle_X$.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[lem-ip-tv-dual-attainment-and-certificate-limit]]: every supplied global minimizer has $p_{\alpha,w}=(f+w-Au_{\alpha,w})/\alpha$, the exact-data fields $p_{\alpha,0}$ remain bounded as $\alpha\to0$, and $\|p_{\alpha,w}-p_{\alpha,0}\|_Y\le\|w\|_Y/\alpha$.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[lem-ip-bv-compactness-lower-semicontinuity]]: bounded-domain BV sequences with bounded $L^1$ norm and variation have an $L^1$-convergent subsequence, and TV is lower semicontinuous under $L^1$ convergence.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[lem-ip-bv-sobolev-inequality]]: in two dimensions, $\|v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}\le TV(v;\mathbb R^2)$ for $v\in BV(\mathbb R^2)$.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[lem-ip-tv-l2-sobolev-inequality]]: the same estimate holds for $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ with finite extended variation: $\|u\|_2\le TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)$.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[lem-ip-bv-zero-gradient-constant-on-connected-domain]]: a locally integrable function with zero distributional gradient on a connected open domain is a.e. constant.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[def-ip-boundary-tv-conventions]]: Neumann TV is unchanged by adding constants; Dirichlet TV is the full-space TV of the zero extension and dominates the interior variation.

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] [[lem-ip-bv-test-field-characterization-and-lsc]]: spatial TV is lower semicontinuous in $L^1$ and finite whenever the extended test-field variation is finite under Countable Choice.

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] [[lem-ip-tv-l2-finite-variation-has-radon-derivative]]: finite $TV_2$ gives a finite vector Radon derivative measure, whose restriction to bounded balls has variation at most $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)$.

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] [[thm-bolzano-weierstrass]]: bounded scalar real sequences have convergent subsequences.

facts.label: F11
facts.text: [F11] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]: $|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\|y\|$.

facts.label: F12
facts.text: [F12] [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]: bounded linear functionals on a real Hilbert space are inner products with vectors in that space.

facts.label: F13
facts.text: [F13] [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]: two locally integrable functions that define the same distribution are equal almost everywhere.

facts.label: F14
facts.text: [F14] [[lem-ip-neumann-bv-sobolev-poincare]]: on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ for a fixed finite $C_\Omega$.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable Choice is used by the coarea, BV representation, and compactness suppliers. ([[def-countable-choice]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[lem-ip-tv-dual-attainment-and-certificate-limit]]: each supplied minimizer has $p_n=(f+w_n-Au_n)/\alpha_n$, $v_n=A^*p_n\in\partial TV(u_n)\cap\partial TV(0)$, the exact-data fields $v_{\alpha_n,0}$ converge strongly in $L^2$ to $v_0$, and $\|v_n-v_{\alpha_n,0}\|_2\le\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n\le\eta$.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate]]: the initial exact truth is minimum-TV and the source certificate supplies a subgradient in the real Hilbert pairing.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-ip-tv-level-set-representatives-and-boundaries]]: for $t>0$ use the density-one representative of $\{u>t\}$; for $t<0$ use that of $\{u<t\}$; bounded-domain sets are viewed by zero extension solely for their ambient geometry.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[lem-ip-tv-l2-coarea-formula]] and [[lem-ip-bv-coarea-formula]]: full-space finite-variation $L^2$ functions and bounded-domain BV functions have the corresponding positive-superlevel/negative-sublevel coarea identities.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[def-ip-tv-variational-curvature]]: variational curvature means minimization of the branch-specific perimeter minus the signed integral of its curvature over compactly supported symmetric-difference perturbations.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[lem-ip-planar-isoperimetric-inequality-for-finite-perimeter-sets]]: $4\pi|E|\le P(E;\mathbb R^2)^2$ for finite-area finite-perimeter planar sets.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[lem-ip-neumann-bv-sobolev-poincare]]: on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ for the stated Neumann constant.

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] [[lem-ip-bv-test-field-characterization-and-lsc]]: the spatial test-field variation is lower semicontinuous under $L^1$ convergence and equals perimeter on finite-perimeter indicators.

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] [[thm-bolzano-weierstrass]]: every bounded scalar real sequence has a convergent subsequence. Applying it to the first coordinate and then to the second coordinate of that subsequence gives a convergent subsequence in $\mathbb R^2$, since the first-coordinate convergence is retained.

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] Actual ball-cut and obstacle comparisons, uniform two-sided density in all three branches, and a common full-space support bound follow from distributional ball products and radial-tail extinction. [[lem-ip-tv-finite-perimeter-ball-cut-calculus]], [[lem-ip-tv-uniform-density-and-radial-support-for-curvature-minimizers]]

facts.label: F12
facts.text: [F12] The distributional L2 TV is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous and positively one-homogeneous, and agrees with BV TV on integrable functions. [[lem-ip-tv-l2-functional-properties]]

facts.label: F11
facts.text: [F11] A bounded Lipschitz-domain BV indicator has a BV zero extension, so its ambient perimeter is finite even in the Neumann branch. Completed Fubini and Tonelli apply to the signed layer-cake integrals when their absolute integral is finite. [[lem-ip-bv-lipschitz-trace-and-zero-extension]], [[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]

facts.label: F13
facts.text: [F13] The real Hilbert pairing satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz. [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]

facts.text: [A1] Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, means every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function. ([[def-countable-choice]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-ip-2d-radon-transform]]: $Rf$ is the line integral of $f$ in the $\theta^\perp$ direction; $|D_s|$ has multiplier $2\pi|\sigma|$ and $|D|^{-1}$ has multiplier $(2\pi|\xi|)^{-1}$ in the inverse Fourier integral.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[thm-ip-fourier-slice-identity]]: for compactly supported smooth $f$, $\widehat{Rf}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat f(\sigma\theta)$ for every $\theta\in S^1$ and $\sigma\in\mathbb R$.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]: under Countable Choice, the polar surface set function on $S^1$ is $\mu(E)=2\lambda_2(\{r\theta:\theta\in E,\ 0<r\le1\})$ for Borel $E$.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]: under Countable Choice, $\mu$ is a finite Borel measure and $\int_{\mathbb R^2}h(\xi)\,d\lambda_2(\xi)=\int_0^\infty\int_{S^1}h(r\theta)r\,d\mu(\theta)\,dr$ for every nonnegative Borel $h$.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]]: under Countable Choice, an invertible linear map $T$ satisfies $\lambda_2(T[E])=|\det T|\lambda_2(E)$ for every Lebesgue measurable $E$.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[thm-fourier-transform-maps-schwartz-space-continuously-to-itself]]: under Countable Choice, the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier transform maps $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ continuously to itself.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[thm-fourier-inversion-on-schwartz-space]]: under Countable Choice, $u(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\widehat u(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\xi$ for every $u\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, with absolute convergence.

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]: under Countable Choice, the compact-support Riemann and Lebesgue integrals agree for smooth compactly supported test integrands and their bounded Borel zero extensions.

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]: absolutely integrable complex functions on sigma-finite product measure spaces have equal product and iterated integrals.

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]: the Lebesgue integral is complex-linear on $L^1$.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) is used by the smooth partition of unity and the countable Fubini realization of weak derivatives on coordinate boxes. No full Axiom of Choice is invoked.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The metric is smooth and positive definite, $dV_g$ is its Riemannian density, $d_g$ is the infimum-of-lengths metric on a connected manifold, and $\Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\nabla_g$. ([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]], [[def-riemannian-volume-density]], [[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]], [[def-riemannian-speed-and-length]], [[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For every nonempty $K$, $d_g(\cdot,K)$ is 1-Lipschitz with respect to $d_g$. ([[lem-distance-to-set-is-lipschitz]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] In a smooth chart, the length of a coordinate line segment $z(s)=z_0+sa$ is $\int\sqrt{g_{z(s)}(a,a)}\,ds$. On compact subcharts the coordinate metric is uniformly comparable to the Euclidean metric. ([[def-riemannian-speed-and-length]], [[lem-local-comparison-of-a-riemannian-metric-with-the-euclidean-metric]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Under Countable Choice, a Lipschitz function on a coordinate box is absolutely continuous on almost every line in each fixed direction and has an almost-everywhere integrable line derivative. Fubini and difference quotients identify that derivative as a weak directional derivative: for a compactly supported smooth test $\phi$, translate by $h$ in the chosen direction, change variables, and let $h\to0$; the difference quotients of the Lipschitz function are bounded, converge to its derivative almost everywhere, and dominated convergence applies. On a boundary half-box reflect the Lipschitz function across the flat face to apply this interior argument; on a half-interval the same bounded difference quotients give $\int_a^b f'=f(b)-f(a)$, because $h^{-1}\int_a^b(f(x+h)-f(x))dx\to f(b)-f(a)$; applying this to the Lipschitz product $f\phi$ gives the endpoint integration-by-parts term. Weak derivatives are linear and unique almost everywhere. ([[thm-c1-lipschitz-ac-bv-hierarchy]], [[thm-absolutely-continuous-functions-have-integrable-derivatives]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]], [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[lem-weak-derivative-linearity-locality-and-commutation]], [[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] An invertible linear change of Euclidean coordinates preserves null sets and transforms weak directional derivatives by the corresponding linear combination. ([[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[lem-weak-derivative-linearity-locality-and-commutation]])

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The Riemannian divergence and boundary pairing for smooth vector fields are given by the coordinate divergence formula and the Green identity on $M$. ([[lem-ip-riemannian-green-boundary-traces-and-wave-lifting]])

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] A smooth partition of unity subordinate to a boundary-compatible coordinate cover exists under Countable Choice. ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds-with-boundary]])

facts.label: A2

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-ip-transversally-anisotropic-product-domain]]: $g=dx_1^2\oplus g_0$ and $\Delta_g=\partial_{x_1}^2+\Delta_{g_0}$.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[lem-ip-limiting-carleman-estimate-on-product]]: for $\varphi=x_1$, the conjugated operator $P_{\varphi,h,q}=e^{\varphi/h}h^2(-\Delta_g+q)e^{-\varphi/h}$ has a distributional right inverse on $L^2$ with norm at most $C h^{-1}$.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-riemannian-gradient]] and [[def-laplace-beltrami-operator-as-trace-of-the-hessian]]: the product metric extends the gradient bilinearly to complex phases, and $\Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\nabla_g$.

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] [[lem-ip-limiting-carleman-estimate-on-product]] supplies only an $L^2$ distributional right inverse, so it does not establish $r_\tau\in H^1(M)$ up to $\partial M$. The needed estimate would be an $H^1_{\mathrm{scl}}$ right inverse for $e^{x_1/h}h^2(-\Delta_g+q)e^{-x_1/h}$ with norm $O(h^{-1})$, which yields $\|r_\tau\|_{H^1_{\mathrm{scl}}}=O(h)$ for the CGO residual and hence the stated $L^2$ bound. Dos Santos Ferreira–Kenig–Salo–Uhlmann, Proposition 4.4, states this type of $H^1$ solvability, but its printed proof invokes “Lemma 4.9 applied to $P_\varphi^*$”; no such lemma appears in that paper. Its reference [27] is Sharafutdinov's *Integral Geometry of Tensor Fields*, whose §4.9 is bibliographical remarks, not the required shifted estimate. Dos Santos Ferreira–Kurylev–Lassas–Salo, Proposition 2.1, states the $H^1$ output but explicitly derives it from the earlier Carleman source and gives no independent proof. Thus no complete verified supplier argument is presently available here.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The volume model defines $K_{q,k}$ on complex $L^2(D)$ by the outgoing kernel, treats inputs as equivalence classes, sets the diagonal representative to zero, and uses $|q|\le\|q\|_\infty$ almost everywhere ([[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For $\operatorname{diam}(D)<\infty$, $\|K_{q,k}\|_{L^2\to L^2}\le C_D\|q\|_\infty$, where $C_D=\sqrt{M\operatorname{diam}(D)/(4\pi)}$ ([[lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The plane wave has modulus one, so its restriction to $D$ is in $L^2(D)$ with norm $\sqrt M$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] If $\rho_k(q)<1$ and $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$, then $u=f+K_{q,k}u$ has a unique solution in $L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ ([[thm-volume-integral-scattering-born-neumann-error]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For $a,b\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$, the pairing is representative-independent and $|\int_D a\overline b|\le\|a\|_2\|b\|_2$ ([[thm-complex-l-two-inner-product-is-well-defined-and-cauchy-schwarz]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] For $g\in L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, $\widehat g(\xi)=\int g(y)e^{-2\pi i y\cdot\xi}\,dy$ is absolutely convergent at every $\xi$ and unchanged by null-set modifications ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[lem-l-one-fourier-transform-is-well-defined]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] For a measurable representative with finite essential norm, $|q|\le\|q\|_\infty$ almost everywhere ([[prop-essential-supremum-is-attained-as-the-least-essential-bound]]).

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$, the far-field map is continuous in observation direction and its values are the uniform outgoing-wave limits of the exterior volume potential, with the displayed explicit remainder ([[lem-volume-far-field-map-is-bounded]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable Choice is assumed by the volume model and the Neumann theorem used here ([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.text: [F1] The definition fixes $K_{q,k}$, $\rho_k(q)$, $\mathcal S_k(q)$, and $\mathcal B_kq$ on the stated quotient spaces and gives $C_D=\sqrt{M\operatorname{diam}(D)/(4\pi)}$ ([[def-ip-fixed-frequency-far-field-data]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The volume operator is linear in $q$ and obeys $\|K_{q,k}\|_{L^2\to L^2}\le C_D\|q\|_\infty$ ([[lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] For $\rho<1$, the unique solution $u=f+K_{q,k}u$ satisfies $\|u-\sum_{j=0}^{N}K_{q,k}^jf\|_2\le \rho^{N+1}\|f\|_2/(1-\rho)$ ([[thm-volume-integral-scattering-born-neumann-error]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The complex L2 pairing is representative-independent and satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz ([[thm-complex-l-two-inner-product-is-well-defined-and-cauchy-schwarz]]).

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Under Countable Choice, $L^\infty(D;\mathbb C)$ is complete; realification leaves its norm and metric unchanged. The same completeness fact applies to $\mathbb C$ as a finite-dimensional complex L-infinity space ([[thm-complex-lp-completeness-and-almost-everywhere-subsequences]], [[lem-complex-norm-realification-is-a-real-norm]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Between real Banach spaces, a Fréchet derivative is a bounded real-linear map whose remainder divided by the input norm tends to zero ([[def-frechet-derivative-between-banach-spaces]], [[def-banach-space]]).

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] For real $t$, $|e^{it}|=1$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]).

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] A measurable representative of the complex contrast satisfies $|q|\le\|q\|_\infty$ almost everywhere ([[prop-essential-supremum-is-attained-as-the-least-essential-bound]]).

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] The domain $\mathcal U_{D,k}$ is open and contains zero ([[lem-ip-small-contrast-scattering-map-well-defined]]).

facts.label: F2

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The constant function $1_D$ is a nonzero vector of $L^2(D)$ with norm $\sqrt{|D|}$, and the complex $L^2$ pairing obeys Cauchy–Schwarz ([[thm-complex-l-two-inner-product-is-well-defined-and-cauchy-schwarz]]).

facts.label: F7

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] The number $\pi$ is positive ([[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]]).

facts.label: F9

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The Axiom of Choice gives a choice function for every family of nonempty sets. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

facts.label: A2
facts.text: [A2] Countable Choice is the restriction of AC to countable families; it is assumed by the Parseval supplier below. [[def-countable-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A probability kernel has a measurable evaluation for every Borel target set and a probability measure at every data point. [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The product sigma-algebra makes the continuous norm and coordinate functions into product-measurable kernel integrands. [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Separability supplies an at-most-countable dense subset of $H$. [[def-separable-space]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A real Hilbert space is complete for its inner-product norm, and a Hilbert basis is a complete orthonormal family. [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For a complete orthonormal family, Parseval's identity equates the squared norm with the sum of squared coordinates; this supplier assumes Countable Choice. [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] A scalar conditional-expectation version is integrable, measurable with respect to its conditioning sigma-algebra, and satisfies the conditioning-event integral identities. [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Under AC, a scalar conditional expectation of an $L^2$ input is its orthogonal projection onto $L^2(\mathcal G)$; in particular its residual is orthogonal to constant random variables. [[thm-conditional-expectation-is-the-l2-orthogonal-projection]]

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] Integrating a product-measurable nonnegative function against a probability kernel gives a measurable function; signed integrals are measurable on their absolute-integrability domain. [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]]

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] Increasing nonnegative measurable functions pass through their integrals by monotone convergence. [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] A measurable action rule with finite posterior risk attaining the pointwise minimum is a Bayes action rule. [[def-posterior-risk-and-bayes-action]]

facts.label: F11
facts.text: [F11] A conditional law is a probability kernel indexed by the conditioning random element; changing its values on a marginal-null set preserves the conditional identities. [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]

facts.label: F12
facts.text: [F12] Integrals of measurable nonnegative or integrable scalar tests against an RCD are conditional-expectation versions. [[thm-conditional-integration-through-a-regular-conditional-law]]

facts.label: F13
facts.text: [F13] Two integrable scalar versions of the same conditional expectation agree almost surely. [[lem-conditional-expectation-is-unique-almost-surely]]

facts.label: F14
facts.text: [F14] A product of two at-most-countable sets is at most countable. [[thm-product-of-countable]]

facts.label: F15
facts.text: [F15] Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|\langle x,e_j\rangle_H|\le\|x\|_H$ for each unit basis vector $e_j$, so each coordinate functional is continuous; it also gives continuity of the inner product in either argument. [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]

facts.label: F16
facts.text: [F16] A measurable space $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$ has a sigma-algebra $\mathcal Y$ of measurable subsets. [[def-measurable-space]]

external_boundary.axiom_use: The scalar proximal-selection comparison uses no choice axiom. Its exact-MMSE comparison refers to the locally constructed analytic conditional-mean map.
external_boundary.declared_source_remarks: For $\gamma>0$, a global proximal selection of an extended-real penalty $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ is a map $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every $z\in\mathbb R$, $P(z)$ is a global minimizer of $x\mapsto\frac12|x-z|^2+\gamma h(x)$. The potential $h_{\sigma,\gamma}$ in the exact-MMSE stationarity result is constructed from the conditional-mean map $D_\sigma$. Replacing $D_\sigma$ in PnP-ISTA by an arbitrary map $\widetilde D_\sigma$ does not in general give a global proximal representation or inherit that stationarity conclusion: for every $\gamma>0$, the map $z\mapsto-z$ is not a global proximal selection of any such $h$ that is finite somewhere and nowhere $-\infty$. This does not assert that a particular other denoiser has no different objective.

external_boundary.declared_source_remarks:
Zheng et al.'s InverseBench reports 14 plug-and-play diffusion-prior algorithms and domain-specific baselines on five selected cases: first-Born optical scattering, raw multi-coil knee MRI, black-hole very-long-baseline interferometry, full waveform inversion, and two-dimensional vorticity-form Navier–Stokes inversion. For these experiments, the authors report that diffusion-prior methods often outperform conventional baselines when the training data are suitable, while a classical full-waveform-inversion optimizer initialized from a smoothed ground truth outperforms the tested diffusion-prior methods. In cases with closed-form forward models, methods using more forward-gradient queries can be more accurate and more expensive; the paper reports that this trend fails for its numerical PDE cases. Its Navier–Stokes split has one validation case and ten test cases. The paper reports step-size/Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy (CFL) failures in its PDE experiments. Its Figure 5 out-of-distribution diagnostics feed digit images to a black-hole prior trained on simulated black-hole images, and nine-cell scattering sources to a prior trained on one-to-six-cell sources; for the black-hole case, the authors report outputs with the prior's characteristic ring feature. These are empirical observations for the named data, solvers, methods, tuning protocol, and hardware; they establish no universal ranking, stability bound, posterior exactness, risk-transfer bound, or robustness theorem.

There is a first-Born notation discrepancy between the paper and its released implementation. Appendix B.1 defines a contrast-dependent total field and then displays a sensor equation with that field multiplied by the contrast, which does not itself exhibit a fixed linear map. The pinned implementation instead passes the fixed incident field into the sensor-propagation routine and constructs its cached linear matrix from that fixed field. This page therefore identifies the implemented benchmark as the first-Born linear case and does not infer linearity from the printed contrast-dependent expression.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The integrating factor $e^{t/2}$ in the scalar forward equation gives $X_t=e^{-t/2}X_0+e^{-t/2}\int_0^t e^{u/2}\,dW_u$. The stochastic integral is the mean-square limit of deterministic dyadic sums of independent Gaussian increments; these sums are centered Gaussian, with variances tending to $\int_0^te^u\,du=e^t-1$, and are independent of $X_0$. The limit is therefore Gaussian with that variance and independent of $X_0$, as follows by taking limits of its Gaussian characteristic functions. At time $t$, the noised target is the symmetric Gaussian mixture with means $\pm e^{-t/2}a$ and common variance $v_t=e^{-t}v+1-e^{-t}>0$. Its exact score is a posterior-weighted average of $-(x-e^{-t/2}a)/v_t$ and $-(x+e^{-t/2}a)/v_t$, so $|s_t(x)|\le(|x|+a)/\min\{v,1\}$ and is continuous. These formulas follow directly by differentiating the sum of the two Gaussian densities.

facts.label: A2
facts.text: [A2] A convolution with a nondegenerate Gaussian has a strictly positive continuous density: continuity follows from the bounded Gaussian derivative, and positivity from its positive kernel. Gaussian densities have finite first moments and exponentially decaying tails.

facts.label: F3

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] For real $t$, $|t|\ge0$, $|-t|=|t|$, and $|t|=0$ exactly when $t=0$ ([[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] A nonnegative real has a unique nonnegative square root ([[thm-of-square-roots]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Every real square is nonnegative ([[lem-of-square-positive]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] The real order is total, so every two-element set of real numbers has a least element, which is its minimum ([[def-ordered-field]], [[def-max-min]]).

facts.text: [F1] [[def-ip-real-frame-phase-retrieval]]: phase retrieval means injectivity of the intensity map on classes modulo one global sign; the real measurement at label $i$ is $\langle a_i,x\rangle$.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[lem-ip-real-phase-retrieval-quotient-metric]]: the induced intensity map is well defined on those classes, and $[x]=[z]$ exactly when $x=z$ or $x=-z$.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-ip-frame-complement-property]]: the complement property requires that for each $S\subseteq[m]$, the span indexed by $S$ or the span indexed by its complement is all of $\mathbb R^d$.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-standard-bilinear-form-on-a-coordinate-space]], [[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]: the real coordinate pairing is bilinear and positive definite; $v\in U^\perp$ means its pairing with every vector of $U$ is zero.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[def-linear-combination-and-span]], [[def-linear-subspace]]: the span of a set is a linear subspace containing that set, and every vector in the span is a finite linear combination of its generators.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[lem-the-orthogonal-complement-of-a-subspace-under-the-standard-form]]: for a subspace $U\le\mathbb R^d$, $\dim U^\perp=d-\dim U$.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace]]: a subspace $U$ of the finite-dimensional space $\mathbb R^d$ has $\dim U=d$ exactly when $U=\mathbb R^d$.

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] [[def-dimension]]: a positive finite dimension supplies a nonempty finite basis, hence a nonzero vector.

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] [[thm-reals-field]]: the real numbers form a field, so a nonzero real scalar such as $2$ cannot annihilate a nonzero vector over $\mathbb R$.

facts.label: F9

facts.label: F5

facts.text: [F6] For $P\ll Q$ with RN derivative $r$, $D(P\|Q)=\int r\log r\,dQ$ with $0\log0=0$ and finite negative part; on a probability space, $\int (r\log r)^-\,dQ\le1/e$. [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, asserts that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-ip-discrete-linear-input-state-output-experiment]]: states obey $x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k$, outputs obey $y_k=Cx_k$, and observation errors are additive deterministic vectors.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[thm-matrix-multiplication-laws]]: compatible matrix products are associative, identity matrices act on either side, and multiplication distributes over finite sums.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-rank-and-nullity]]: $\operatorname{rank}T=\dim(\operatorname{im}T)$ and $\operatorname{nullity}T=\dim(\ker T)$ for finite-dimensional domains.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[thm-rank-nullity]]: for a linear map with finite-dimensional domain, $\dim V=\operatorname{nullity}T+\operatorname{rank}T$.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]]: a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner-product spaces has orthonormal left and right singular bases, with its positive singular values ordered nonincreasingly.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[cor-rank-equals-number-of-nonzero-singular-values]]: the rank equals the number of positive singular values.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]]: $O^+$ satisfies $OO^+O=O$, $O^+OO^+=O^+$, and $OO^+$ and $O^+O$ are self-adjoint.

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] [[thm-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse-exists-and-is-unique]]: every finite real matrix has a unique Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] [[prop-full-column-rank-pseudoinverse-formula]]: if $O$ has full column rank, then $O^+O=I_d$.

facts.label: F10
facts.text: [F10] [[thm-aa-plus-and-a-plus-a-are-orthogonal-projections-onto-the-image-spaces]]: $OO^+$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}O$.

facts.label: F11
facts.text: [F11] [[thm-a-plus-b-is-the-unique-minimum-norm-least-squares-solution]]: for a finite real matrix $O$ and vector $b$, $O^+b$ is the unique least-squares solution of minimum Euclidean norm.

facts.label: F12
facts.text: [F12] [[lem-pythagorean-theorem-and-finite-orthogonal-sums]]: if $a$ and $b$ are orthogonal, then $\|a+b\|_2^2=\|a\|_2^2+\|b\|_2^2$.

facts.text: [L1] Full AC supplies Countable Choice: for any sequence $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of nonempty sets, apply AC to the family $\{X_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ and set $f(n)=c(X_n)$ for its choice function $c$. facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]] defines $K$ as a smooth embedding of an oriented circle in the standard oriented $S^3$.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[prop-the-image-of-a-smooth-embedding-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] identifies the image of a smooth embedding as an embedded submanifold; here its local charts are intervals, so the image is locally contractible.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-knot-exterior]] fixes $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and the ambient orientation.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]] defines the positive meridian as the oriented boundary of a normal disk and a preferred longitude as a degree-one parallel curve with zero image in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] [[lem-knot-tubular-exterior-and-boundary]] supplies a product tubular map on a slightly larger disk bundle, the exterior retraction, and the product torus coordinates.

facts.label: F9

facts.label: F10

facts.label: F12

facts.label: F13

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A regular diagram is the image of an oriented link under a projection whose only multiple points are finitely many transverse double points, with no triple points; its strands carry their orientations and over/under data ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] At a crossing $c$, $\operatorname{sgn}(c)$ is the sign of the determinant of the oriented overpassing and underpassing projected tangent vectors in the oriented projection plane ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] For compact boundaryless sources, the mod $2$ intersection number of two transverse maps is the cardinality of their fiber product with coefficients in $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$; it is invariant under homotopy of either map when $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ holds ([[def-mod-two-intersection-number]], [[thm-mod-two-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two regular oriented diagrams represent the same oriented link if and only if a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves of types I, II, and III connects them ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] A type-I move creates or deletes one self-crossing; a type-II move creates or deletes two crossings of opposite sign; a type-III move preserves the signs and over/under data of its three crossings ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).
