facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); it implies $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]].

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] For one oriented component $K$, Alexander duality identifies $H_1(S^3\setminus K;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z$ by the total-linking homomorphism, and a positively oriented meridian $\eta$ maps to $1$; hence $[\eta]$ generates this homology group ([[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]], Facts & Assumptions [F2], [F7]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The complement $X$ is path-connected, and the first Hurewicz map identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the abelianization of $\pi_1(X)$ ([[lem-the-complement-of-an-oriented-link-is-a-connected-smooth-three-manifold]], [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The oriented intersection number of complementary-dimensional maps is the signed sum of the local determinant-orientation signs and is invariant under homotopy of transverse maps; the proof counts the oriented boundary of a compact oriented one-manifold ([[def-oriented-intersection-number]], [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]], [[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Under the Axiom of Choice, transversality can be achieved while fixing a neighborhood of a closed region where the map is already transverse; a transverse homotopy has a compact oriented one-manifold as its preimage of $\Sigma$, with boundary at the endpoint intersections and total signed boundary count zero ([[prop-relative-transversality-preserves-a-map-on-a-closed-good-region]], [[thm-transverse-preimage-for-manifolds-with-boundary]], [[lem-oriented-boundary-of-a-compact-oriented-one-manifold-has-zero-signed-count]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a continuous map between smooth manifolds that is smooth near a closed subset has a smooth approximation homotopic to it relative to a neighborhood of that subset ([[thm-relative-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The diagram algorithm returns half the sum of mixed crossing signs, and the sign is the determinant of the oriented over and under tangents in the oriented projection plane ([[alg-oriented-linking-number-from-diagram]], [[thm-oriented-linking-number-scan-terminates-and-is-correct]], [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] The standard smooth step function is constant on collars of the endpoints of its unit interval ([[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A regular diagram is an immersion with finitely many transverse double points, no triple points, and finitely many component arcs ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Each crossing sign is the determinant sign of its oriented over and under projected tangents in the oriented projection plane ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The blackboard vector is the nonzero normal section given by the positive quarter-turn of the projected oriented tangent ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A smooth map between manifolds of the same dimension with invertible differential at a point is a diffeomorphism on suitable neighborhoods of that point ([[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the normal quotient has its smooth vector-bundle structure; a tubular chart is a diffeomorphism fixed on the zero section, and its normalization makes the vertical differential the identity on the normal quotient ([[prop-normal-and-conormal-bundles-are-smooth-vector-bundles]], [[def-tubular-neighbourhood-of-an-embedded-submanifold]], [[cor-tubular-neighbourhoods-are-unique-up-to-ambient-isotopy]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every sufficiently small push-off along a smooth nowhere-zero normal section is an embedded circle disjoint from the original knot ([[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Every open cover of a compact metric space has a positive Lebesgue number, so sufficiently close parameters lie together in one member of a finite cover ([[thm-lebesgue-number-lemma]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The self-linking number of a framed knot is the linking number with a sufficiently small embedded push-off along its framing section ([[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]], [[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]]).

facts.label: F2

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The blackboard push-off has exactly two mixed crossings of the original sign for each original self-crossing and no other mixed crossings ([[lem-blackboard-push-off-has-two-mixed-crossings-per-crossing]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, ambient-isotopic regular oriented link diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A type-I move adds or removes a self-crossing; type II adds or removes two crossings of opposite signs; type III preserves the signs of its three crossings ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Writhe is the signed sum over all crossings, and self-writhe is the signed sum over one component's self-crossings ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Linking number is the integer half-sum of mixed crossing signs, invariant under all three Reidemeister moves ([[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For a knot, blackboard self-linking equals diagram writhe ([[thm-blackboard-framing-self-linking-is-writhe]]).

facts.label: F2

facts.label: F3

facts.label: F4

facts.text: [A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is assumed. Only the smooth disk-attachment and isotopy-extension suppliers below use it; every geometric selection in this proof is finite.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A smooth map with invertible derivative is a local diffeomorphism, without a choice hypothesis ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A simple polygon has exactly one bounded complementary region and one unbounded complementary region, with the polygon as the frontier of both ([[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A simple polygonal region has a finite straight triangulation ([[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]]), and a connected finite plane graph has $V-E+F=2$ ([[thm-euler-formula-for-connected-plane-graphs]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Under Countable Choice, attaching a standard smooth disk along an embedded boundary disk, with the corner rounded, preserves the diffeomorphism type ([[lem-boundary-connected-sum-with-a-disk-does-not-change-the-diffeomorphism-type]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Under Countable Choice, an isotopy of embeddings of a compact smooth manifold with boundary into a boundaryless manifold of the same dimension, constant near the two time endpoints, extends to a smooth ambient isotopy supported in any specified neighborhood of its track ([[lem-isotopy-extension-for-a-compact-source-with-boundary]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For a knot with a supplied oriented spanning surface, the inward unit surface conormal is a reference normal framing, and relative winding identifies its framing class with zero. ([[thm-oriented-knot-framing-classes-form-z-torsor]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the inward unit conormal defines the Seifert framing; its self-linking is the linking number with a sufficiently small push-off along that section. ([[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The linking number of a framed knot is unchanged when its normal section is replaced by a homotopic nowhere-zero section and the push-off radius is sufficiently small. ([[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For disjoint oriented circles $J,K$ and an oriented spanning surface $\Sigma$ with $\partial\Sigma=K$, if $J$ is transverse to $\Sigma$ and $D$ is a regular oriented diagram of $J\cup K$, the diagram linking number equals the signed intersection number $J\cdot\Sigma$. The theorem assumes the Axiom of Choice. ([[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]])

facts.text: [F1] For a smooth map from a boundaryless manifold to a boundaryless target, there is a finite-dimensional smooth perturbation family through that map whose parameter map is a submersion at every source point. facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] If a smooth family $G:X\times B\to M$ is transverse to $S$, then the parameters for which the slice $G_a:X\to M$ is not transverse to $S$ form a null subset of $B$. ([[thm-parametric-transversality]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar. ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Under AC$_\omega$, every smooth isotopy of embeddings of a compact source with boundary into a boundaryless target extends to an ambient isotopy. ([[thm-isotopy-extension]])

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Under AC$_\omega$, every smooth manifold, including one with boundary, admits a Riemannian metric compatible with its manifold topology. ([[thm-every-smooth-manifold-admits-a-riemannian-metric]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A regular embedded nullhomotopic circle in an oriented surface bounds an embedded compact disk region under countable choice ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], clause 4). In the plane its nullhomotopy is the linear contraction. For smooth input the disk is smooth: the disk-and-band construction in steps 7.1–12.1 of [[lem-finite-c2-surface-carriers-have-smooth-normal-forms-and-relative-cap-approximations]] uses smooth collars, smooth interval maps and smooth circle-map extensions throughout. Thus its smooth-input construction gives a smooth disk parametrization, including a prescribed smooth boundary collar.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The local form at a nondegenerate surface critical point is $z=z(p)\pm u^2\pm v^2$ ([[thm-morse-lemma]]). A compact smooth embedding isotopy extends to a compactly supported ambient isotopy under countable choice ([[thm-isotopy-extension]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A generic linear height on a compact Euclidean embedded smooth manifold is Morse ([[thm-generic-height-functions-on-an-embedded-compact-manifold-are-morse]]). Its finitely many critical values can be separated by arbitrarily small local bump perturbations without changing its critical points or Hessians ([[lem-finitely-many-critical-values-can-be-separated-locally]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Under countable choice a regular nullhomotopic circle on an oriented surface bounds a compact disk; on a sphere both complementary closures are disk regions ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], clause 4). In the plane use the explicit linear contraction. Smooth disk parametrizations, including collar-compatible boundary maps, are obtained by the smooth-input disk-and-band construction in steps 7.1–13.1 of [[lem-finite-c2-surface-carriers-have-smooth-normal-forms-and-relative-cap-approximations]]. In particular the two disks obtained by cutting a smooth sphere along a regular circle are smooth disks.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Each sphere obtained by capping a height piece with at most one critical point bounds a smooth standard ball ([[lem-capped-elementary-height-spheres-bound-smooth-balls]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A disk attachment or its reverse is absorbed without changing the smooth manifold type, and an embedded standard ball is ambient isotopic to a coordinate round ball ([[lem-smooth-ball-windows-and-boundary-disk-absorption]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Smooth isotopies of compact embedded submanifolds extend to ambient isotopies under countable choice ([[thm-isotopy-extension]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable choice is [[def-countable-choice]]. Its use is inherited from the local disk, smooth normal-form and isotopy-extension suppliers [F2]–[F5]; it is an assumption of this local proof, not a claim that the classical theorem requires that axiom intrinsically. The surgeries and their reversal form finite constructions.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A compact TOP three-manifold has a finite combinatorial PL triangulation. Prescribed finite boundary PL structures and TOP collars are retained on smaller collars. The proof constructs the actual finite atlas by compact-overlap handle straightening. [[thm-compact-topological-three-manifolds-admit-finite-pl-triangulations]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For every index, a TOP coordinate embedding of a PL three-dimensional handle, PL near its attaching boundary, admits an ambient source TOP isotopy fixed there and outside twice its compact core, making the endpoint PL near the prescribed FIXED core. The finite PL vertex/edge/face/tetrahedron handle construction is given in [F1], Proof1.1, and its attaching-band protection in Proof2.1. [[thm-three-dimensional-topological-handles-admit-relative-pl-straightenings]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A supplied finite orientable PL three-manifold has a finite prime connected-sum presentation with original boundary marks, actual cap parameters and gluing maps. Its nonirreducible prime factors are standard $S^1\times S^2$, which is PL prime; the other factors are PL irreducible. Its Proof1.1 gives finite cap-ball avoidance, and Proof3.1 gives the actual marked nonseparating-sphere handle model. No uniqueness is assumed. [[thm-finite-orientable-pl-three-manifolds-have-prime-connected-sum-decompositions]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Finite PL Schoenflies in the standard three-sphere, finite marked ball-window gluing, and compatible finite convex-cell triangulations hold. A PL sphere boundary map extends over a parametrized ball by coning; the same formula extends any TOP sphere boundary map over a TOP parametrized ball. [[thm-finite-pl-schoenflies-in-dimension-three]] [[lem-parametrized-pl-balls-absorb-standard-boundary-windows]] [[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] A compact TOP three-manifold with its finite triangulated boundary has a TOP product collar. [[lem-compact-topological-three-manifolds-with-triangulated-boundary-have-collars]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Finite simplicial chains compute singular homology, and the open-cover Mayer–Vietoris sequence is exact. [[thm-simplicial-and-singular-homology-agree-for-simplicial-complexes]] [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Continuous maps of finite polyhedral pairs admit simplicial approximations homotopic as maps of pairs; PL maps admit compatible finite subdivisions ([[thm-finite-simplicial-approximation-for-maps-of-pairs]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A finite subpolyhedron in a finitely triangulated PL three-manifold has a compact PL manifold neighborhood strongly retracting onto it, with controlled trace in a marked boundary subsurface ([[lem-finite-subpolyhedra-have-compact-pl-manifold-neighborhoods]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Compact locally collared PL subpolyhedra have PL collars; in particular this applies to the boundary of a compact PL manifold and to boundary curves of a compact PL surface ([[lem-compact-locally-collared-pl-subpolyhedron-has-pl-collar]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A disk map lifts to any covering after fixing its initial lift ([[thm-covering-space-lifting-criterion]]). Pulling back finitely many triangulation simplices gives a finite compatible PL structure on a twofold cover. Its deck involution sends each point to the other point in the same fiber; its continuity follows by interchanging the two sheets on every evenly covered neighborhood. It has no fixed point.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] If a compact connected orientable finite PL three-manifold has no connected twofold cover, its boundary components are PL spheres. This has a local proof using explicit twofold covers from finite edge cocycles, dual-cell boundary matrices, finite pivots, and finite polygonal surface reduction, with no choice assumption ([[lem-no-twofold-cover-forces-spherical-boundary-in-finite-pl-three-manifold]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] On a PL two-sphere, a simple polygonal circle bounds polygonal disks on its two sides. Finite polygonal disk parametrizations and their boundary extensions are supplied by [[lem-finite-polygonal-disk-and-collar-surgery]] after using a standard two-disk sphere model. A connected compact subsurface is planar; its finitely many boundary components bound the complementary disk regions, as follows by applying the same polygonal separation successively.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] A proper PL disk immersion with only regular double arcs and circles and no values of multiplicity greater than two has an essential embedded disk with respect to any prescribed normal boundary subgroup ([[lem-two-sheeted-pl-disk-immersion-has-essential-embedded-disk]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The actual right-handed trefoil bounds the standard positive two-Hopf-band plumbing, whose positive-push matrix in its ordered core basis is $V=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The handedness and negative diagonal signs are the established geometric convention, not the differently labeled positive matrix in the source-specific KT06 example. [[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix]], [[lem-canonical-positive-three-crossing-braid-has-negative-trefoil-form]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For every knot Seifert surface with the same positive normal and positive-meridian convention, $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\det(V-tV^T)$. The actual boundary connected-sum surface has block matrix $V_K\oplus V_J$: the old bases lie in separated balls and both cross-linking blocks vanish. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[cor-alexander-polynomial-multiplies-under-connected-sum]], Proof2.1–4.1.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] At every nonroot point $\omega$, the signature of $(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$ is an oriented knot invariant independent of surface and basis. The full knot-surface S-equivalence and stabilization proofs now establish this actual interface. [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]], [[lem-seifert-matrices-of-a-knot-are-s-equivalent]], [[lem-seifert-stabilization-preserves-levine-tristram-signature]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The right trefoil is prime, reflection preserves nontriviality and primality, and the oriented prime decomposition is unique up to ordering and insertion/deletion of unknot factors. [[lem-right-trefoil-is-prime]], [[lem-mirroring-preserves-primality-of-a-knot]], [[thm-schubert-prime-decomposition-for-knots]], [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypothesis used by the supplied surface normal-form theorem: for a sequence of nonempty sets, apply the AC choice function to its range and use the chosen element on each index. [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The supplied surface is connected, compact, smooth, oriented, and has boundary the oriented knot; its genus satisfies $\chi(F)=1-2g$. [[def-oriented-seifert-surface]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Under the countable-choice interface, a compact genus-$g$ surface with one boundary component has $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2g}$ and standard handle generators represented by simple smooth curves. Resolving finitely many transverse crossings in a cycle inside small oriented disks preserves its homology class and gives a disjoint-union representative. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] For a disjoint oriented circle $J$ and an oriented circle $L$, the linking number is the coefficient of the positive meridian in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$; the positive meridian maps to $1$ under the Alexander-duality normalization. The coefficient map is a homomorphism. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The local oriented intersection sign is the sign of the determinant of the ordered tangent and normal bases. [[def-oriented-intersection-number]], [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] If an oriented circle is supplied with a compact oriented spanning surface and a regular diagram of the two-component link, the positive-meridian linking coefficient equals the signed intersection count with that surface. [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

facts.label: F6

facts.text: [F1] At each crossing, based positive meridians on the source and target under-sides satisfy the side-based conjugation relation. [[lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjugacy]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] In the meridian basis of [F3], the class of a word is its vector of meridian exponent sums. Positive arc meridians on the same component differ by tube transport and conjugation, hence have the same homology class. The choice-free first Hurewicz theorem identifies loop concatenation with addition in $H_1$ and kills conjugation. facts.label: F4

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The one-variable Alexander module is first homology of the cover classified by total linking, whose defining map sums the Alexander-dual meridian coordinates ([[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]).

facts.label: F7

facts.label: F8

facts.label: F9

facts.text: [F3] [[lem-torus-knot-alexander-polynomial-from-presentation]] proves that the positive-meridian Alexander module is cyclic with order $\delta_{p,q}(t)=(t^{pq}-1)(t-1)/((t^p-1)(t^q-1))$, a Laurent polynomial, and hence $\Delta_K\doteq\delta_{p,q}$.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] [[lem-positive-torus-knot-hopf-plumbing-surface]] constructs a positive Hopf-plumbed Seifert surface of genus $(a-1)(b-1)/2$ for $T(a,b)$ when $a,b\ge2$.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] [[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]] defines $g(K)$ as the minimum genus of a connected compact oriented spanning surface under Countable Choice.

facts.label: F8

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] **External input — Loop Theorem.** If a subsurface $F$ of the boundary of a compact $3$-manifold $N$ has noninjective $\pi_1(F)\to\pi_1(N)$, an essential simple closed curve in $F$ bounds a properly embedded disk in $N$. Source: Aschenbrenner–Friedl–Wilton, *3-Manifold Groups*, arXiv:1205.0202, Theorem 1.2, p.7.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] **External input — comparison of atoroidality conventions.** For compact orientable irreducible $3$-manifolds with empty or toroidal boundary, the condition that every incompressible embedded torus is boundary-parallel and the condition that every $\pi_1$-injective torus map is homotopic into the boundary agree outside certain Seifert-fibered manifolds. In particular they agree for a manifold which is not Seifert-fibered. Source: the same survey, §1.4, p.9, immediately after its definition of atoroidal. This is the torus-theorem consequence expressly recorded there; it is imported, not reconstructed here.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] **External input — Hyperbolization Theorem.** If $N$ is compact, orientable, irreducible, has empty or toroidal boundary, is atoroidal in the torus-map convention, and has infinite fundamental group, then its interior admits a complete hyperbolic metric. For this empty-or-toroidal-boundary theorem the metric has finite volume. Source: the same survey, Theorem 1.13, p.13, with the definition on p.11 and finite-volume statement/convention on p.12. This imports the complete established hyperbolization result, covering both fibered and nonfibered cases; it does not invoke a conditional deformation theorem to create an initial representation.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **External input — finite-volume cusp decomposition.** A complete oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifold of finite volume is a compact submanifold bounded by tori together with finitely many horoballs modulo rank-two free abelian parabolic actions. Source: Thurston, *The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds*, Chapter 5, Proposition 5.11.1, printed p.116 (PDF p.34). Thus its noncompact ends are exactly its torus cusps.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] There are holomorphic representatives $\rho_u$ and holomorphically varying peripheral eigenlines. On each end a holomorphic change of frame sends that line to $\infty$, and the peripheral maps become $Z\mapsto e^{u_i}Z+a_i(u)$ and $Z\mapsto e^{v_i}Z+b_i(u)$, with $a_i(0)\ne0$, $v_i=\tau_i u_i$ and $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i>0$. facts.label: F2

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The curvature-$-1$ model is the upper half-space $(Z,Y)\in\mathbb C\times(0,\infty)$, with its orientation-preserving projective matrix isometries. facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Ordinary filling attaches a solid torus by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism sending its meridian to the specified slope. Here equality of slopes means equality of unoriented ambient-isotopy classes of embedded curves on the torus, the standard ordinary-slope convention. A boundary homeomorphism between product solid tori extends core-preservingly, with the same orientation sign, if an ambient isotopy of the target boundary moves the image meridian to its target meridian. facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypotheses of the smooth approximation, ODE and transversality suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A locally flat surface has the pair charts and prescribed boundary collars in the Definition. For a smooth surface these are smooth charts. The Definition alone does not assert a global TOP normal disk bundle. [[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Local smooth ODEs, the inverse-function theorem and Euclidean smooth approximation apply with compact parameters. Parametric transversality applies to finite smooth perturbation families. [[thm-time-dependent-vector-fields-have-local-smooth-evolution-operators]], [[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]], [[thm-whitney-approximation-for-euclidean-valued-maps]], [[thm-parametric-transversality]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Boundary linking equals the intersection of collared bounding chains in the four-ball. Smooth compact manifolds have finite CW homotopy models under countable choice. [[lem-linking-number-equals-four-dimensional-intersection-number]], [[lem-compact-smooth-manifolds-have-finite-cw-models-under-countable-choice]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Mayer–Vietoris computes the actual collared decomposition homology; the oriented meridian is dual to a Seifert surface. [[thm-excision-and-mayer-vietoris-with-local-coefficients]], [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Alexander duality gives the meridional complement class for the capped locally flat surface, but it supplies no regular fiber or collar at that surface. [[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] **External input — relative TOP normal bundle.** Freedman–Quinn, Theorem 9.3A, printed137–141, supplies an actual rank-two normal vector bundle for a locally flat proper surface in a TOP four-manifold, relative to a supplied normal bundle near a closed subset, including a boundary collar. Its neighborhood embedding agrees with that germ after restriction. This is only the normal-bundle input; it does not assert a circle-map fiber or a Seifert hypersurface. The usual full-AC setting of the Statement is retained.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] **External input — strongly relative TOP transversality.** Quinn1988, Theorem printed145: for proper submanifolds $M,X\subset Y$, a specified normal microbundle $\xi$ of $X$, and closed $C\subset D\subset Y$, if $M$ is transverse to $\xi$ near $C$, an isotopy of $M$, supported in any prescribed neighborhood of $(D\setminus C)\cap M\cap X$, makes it transverse near $D$. Boundary properness is part of the theorem. Transversality means that the intersection is a manifold whose normal microbundle in $M$ is the restriction of the specified $\xi$. The theorem includes the dimensions used below, namely $4$-submanifolds of a $5$-manifold with intersection dimension $3$. This theorem is imported, not reconstructed locally.

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] **External input — circle representatives on TOP manifolds.** Metrizable TOP manifolds have CW homotopy type by the ANR/CW-type criterion of Milnor1959. On that homotopy type, Hatcher Proposition1B.9 for $S^1=K(\mathbb Z,1)$ represents every integral first-cohomology class by a continuous map to $S^1$; two such maps with the same induced integer homomorphism are homotopic. These classification inputs are used only to construct a continuous meridian map. They are not transversality assertions.

facts.label: F9
facts.text: [F9] An actual compact TOP manifold with boundary has a TOP product collar of its entire boundary. Apply this only after the exterior has been constructed as such a manifold. [[thm-topological-collaring-for-manifold-boundaries]]

facts.text: [F1] Each annulus is proper, has product collars at its endpoint knots, and has boundary orientation $-K_0\sqcup K_1$ or $-J_0\sqcup J_1$. ([[def-smooth-knot-concordance]], [[def-locally-flat-topological-knot-concordance]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The oriented connected sum is obtained by deleting short trivial arcs and gluing with the fixed orientation-reversing boundary map; its class is independent of the local choices under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $S^3$ is simply connected, continuous homotopies into a smooth manifold can be smoothly approximated relative to a closed region where they are already smooth, finite-dimensional smooth perturbations can be chosen transverse, compact smooth isotopies extend ambiently, and smooth submanifolds have tubular neighborhoods. ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]], [[thm-relative-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps]], [[thm-parametric-transversality]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]], [[def-countable-choice]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Ambient-isotopic oriented knot representatives may be changed by smooth families of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$. A chosen point on a knot can be moved to any prescribed point by an isotopy of embeddings of that point, which extends ambiently under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[def-countable-choice]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Bare locally flat proper arcs with specified product end collars can be straightened by [[thm-locally-flat-codimension-three-arc-unknotting]]. This retained local result is not being strengthened into a relative transverse pair-tube or complement theorem.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] **External TOP input, initially in ordinary ZFC:** connected sum is well-defined on the concordance classes of smooth oriented knots represented by proper locally flat annuli in $S^3\times I$. In particular, the two given annulus concordances imply an oriented locally flat annulus concordance between their endpoint connected sums, in the usual collared-end convention of [F1]. This is the TOP connected-sum operation in Ray, §3, Definition 3.1, Definition 3.5 and the discussion through Proposition 3.6, printed II–11–II–12. It is imported here, not presented as a locally reconstructed pair-tube/complement proof.

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] **External set-theoretic input:** for a real $r\subseteq\omega$, the relativized constructible class $L[r]$ is a transitive inner model of ZFC containing $r$ and all natural numbers. Karagila, §8.3, closing remarks, printed p.42, gives the $L[A]$ construction and its inner-ZFC conclusion; for a real parameter, $r\subseteq\omega\subseteq L[r]$, so the parameter belongs to that model. No ambient full AC is assumed by this input. The compact coding argument below, rather than an implication from ambient full AC, supplies the Countable Choice specialization of [F6].

facts.label: F2

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] An abstract oriented cobordism is a compact oriented surface with boundary $-C_0\sqcup C_1$ and contains no ambient embedding data. ([[def-abstract-oriented-knot-cobordism]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The Seifert matrix convention in the library is $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ for a chosen oriented surface and basis; the surface and basis are part of the data until invariance is proved. ([[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A trefoil Seifert surface admits a rank-two Seifert matrix whose symmetric sum is $\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}$; if the cited convention uses the transpose matrix, the symmetric sum is unchanged. For a real symmetric matrix, its signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues. (Collins, Theorem 2.2.9 and Example 2.2.13, https://era.ed.ac.uk/bitstream/handle/1842/5034/Collins2011.pdf?sequence=4)

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The standard unknot bounds a disk in $S^3$; the disk is contractible, so its first homology is zero and its symmetrized Seifert form has signature $0$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] A metabolizer for a rank-two integral Seifert form is a rank-one direct summand $L$ with $V(x,y)=0$ for $x,y\in L$. Thus every nonzero $x\in L$ satisfies $x^T(V+V^T)x=2V(x,x)=0$. This is immediate from the defining bilinear relation, with no signature-invariance or general signature-vanishing theorem. ([[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]])

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Under the Axiom of Countable Choice, a knot is smoothly slice if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot. ([[lem-smooth-slice-iff-concordant-to-unknot]])

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Full Axiom of Choice is assumed by the supplied Seifert-pairing definition. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

facts.label: A2
facts.text: [A2] Full Axiom of Choice implies the countable-choice hypothesis used by [F6]. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]])

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] For a smooth slice disk, the actual smooth branch of [[lem-slice-disk-induces-seifert-metabolizer]] constructs a metabolizer for every specified smooth Seifert surface: its Proof1.1–2.2 uses the actual smooth hypersurface and positive product constructed in Proof1.1–7.1 of [[lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-seifert-hypersurface]]. The separate unresolved TOP branches are not used here. This direct finite-form obstruction needs neither surface-choice invariance nor a general signature-vanishing theorem.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Full AC is assumed as stated. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The integral group uses finite integral Seifert lattices with unimodular skew part, and the rational group uses the even-dimensional rational isometric structures in the Statement. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]], [[def-integral-witt-and-seifert-isometric-structures]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Integral Seifert classes admit invertible representatives, and the associated rational structure defines an injective homomorphism $\iota:G_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}$. This includes singular-matrix reduction and saturation of rational metabolizers. [[thm-integral-seifert-witt-group-injects-into-rational-isometric-group]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Rational isometric classes split as the direct sum of their self-reciprocal primary groups. For each irreducible $p\ne t+1$ the primary group is the hermitian Witt group of the number field $E=\mathbb Q[t]/(p)$ with involution $t\mapsto t^{-1}$, and the $t+1$ group is the even-dimensional symmetric Witt group over $\mathbb Q$. [[thm-rational-isometric-witt-group-has-reciprocal-primary-decomposition]], [[thm-rational-primary-isometric-classes-are-hermitian-witt-classes]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The kernel of all hermitian signatures over each quadratic number-field extension is killed by four. The rational symmetric signature kernel is also killed by four, including on its even-dimensional subgroup. [[thm-hermitian-number-field-signature-kernel-is-killed-by-four]], [[thm-rational-symmetric-signature-kernel-is-killed-by-four]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The explicit integral matrices $F_b=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&b\end{pmatrix}$, $P_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-n^2\end{pmatrix}$, and $Q_q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-(3q-1)/4\end{pmatrix}$, for $b,n\ge1$ and primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $q\ne3$, lie in distinct quadratic primary components. The first family is independent of infinite order, the second has exact order two, and the third exact order four. The $P_n$ have independent images in $G_{\mathbb Z}/2G_{\mathbb Z}$. [[lem-integral-algebraic-concordance-has-independent-free-two-and-four-torsion-families]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] A countable abelian group mapping to a countable direct sum of copies of $\mathbb Z$ with exponent-four kernel splits into countably many free, order-two, and order-four summands. The three multiplicities are infinite under the precise independent-family tests in that lemma. [[lem-countable-signature-groups-with-exponent-four-kernel-split]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Here the Grothendieck group is defined explicitly using pairs $(E,F)$ of finite-rank smooth complex bundles: $(E,F)$ and $(E',F')$ are equivalent when $E\oplus F'\oplus H\cong E'\oplus F\oplus H$ for some finite-rank smooth bundle $H$. Addition uses direct sums and multiplication uses $(E,F)(E',F')=(E\otimes E'\oplus F\otimes F',E\otimes F'\oplus F\otimes E')$. Bundle distributivity and the tensor flip make this a commutative ring; transitivity follows by adding the two witnessing isomorphisms and including their repeated middle summand in $H$. These formulas are part of the construction, not a claim of cancellation of actual bundles.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The bounding-chain formula is the evaluation pairing obtained by applying the Bockstein inverse to the Poincaré dual of the first torsion class and evaluating on the Poincaré dual of the second. facts.text:
[F2] The infinite cyclic cover and its finite quotient are those defined by the positive-meridian deck action in [[def-infinite-cyclic-cover-of-a-slice-disk-exterior]]. Their chain groups give short exact sequences
$$0\to C_*(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)\xrightarrow{t-1}C_*(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)\to C_*(X_D;\mathbb F_p)\to0$$
and
$$0\to C_*(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)\xrightarrow{t^q-1}C_*(X_{D,\infty};\mathbb F_p)\to C_*(X_{D,q};\mathbb F_p)\to0.$$
Each singular simplex has a free orbit of lifts; quotienting its orbit module by $t-1$ or $t^q-1$ gives the singular chains of the corresponding quotient cover. The long exact homology sequences are supplied by [[thm-long-exact-sequence-in-homology]].

facts.text: [F1] Compact manifold singular chains, with arbitrary based rank-one right-ring coefficients, have explicit domination by bounded finite-free chains. The Wall construction turns such domination into a bounded finite-projective chain homotopy equivalence, with explicit idempotent modules. [[thm-finite-geometric-complex-chains-dominate-compact-manifold-chains-in-zf]], [[lem-choice-free-wall-chain-finiteness-from-explicit-domination]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Oriented cap duality holds on compact collared topological manifolds and their closed boundaries for all underlying abelian-group local systems, with commuting scalar actions. Intrinsic dual cochains are identified with conjugates by the supplied parallel Hermitian form. [[thm-compact-collared-manifold-local-coefficient-lefschetz-duality-in-zf]], [[thm-compact-oriented-manifold-local-coefficient-duality-in-zf]], [[lem-involutive-twisted-chain-duals-realize-local-coefficient-duality]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Finite von Neumann matrix kernels and Hilbert-closed images are projection modules. Quotient dimension is the trace difference of closure projections; dimension-zero modules are closed under submodules, quotients and extensions. Dense injective pullback preserves inertia, and restricting an invertible Hermitian form to a closed coisotropic submodule preserves signature. [[lem-finite-von-neumann-module-dimension-and-dense-quotients]], [[lem-von-neumann-inertia-and-coisotropic-reduction]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Topological equivariant intersections are Hermitian, retain their same-piece values under collared inclusion, and are compatible with the actual support/excision cap comparison. [[lem-relative-unitary-equivariant-intersection-pairing-is-hermitian]], [[lem-equivariant-intersection-pairings-are-preserved-by-collared-bordism-gluing]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Small-chain excision, pair and Mayer–Vietoris sequences hold for the collared gluings. Fundamental classes have finite orientation representatives and compatible local images. The cohomology-first cap convention is $\partial(\alpha\cap z)=(-1)^p(\alpha\cap\partial z-\delta\alpha\cap z)$ for a degree-$p$ cochain. [[thm-excision-and-mayer-vietoris-with-local-coefficients]], [[thm-pair-long-exact-sequences-with-local-coefficients]], [[lem-canonical-twisted-fundamental-classes-over-compact-subsets]], [[def-cup-and-cap-products-with-local-coefficient-pairings]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] A compact connected topological manifold has a finite generating list for its fundamental group without a choice axiom. [[lem-compact-connected-manifold-fundamental-group-has-finite-generators-in-zf]]

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F6

facts.label: F4

facts.label: F6

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] The amalgamated free product of two groups along injective copies of the same subgroup has transversal normal forms. facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A graded Hermitian Clifford module with compatible connection has a chiral Fredholm operator on the exact $H^1\to L^2$ domain, with complex index $\int_X[\widehat A(TX)\operatorname{ch}(V/S)]_4$. Its local multiplicity space has dimension equal to the module rank divided by four in dimension four. The reference chirality is $i^2c(e^1)c(e^2)c(e^3)c(e^4)$. Local multiplicity curvatures and their characters patch even without a global Spin lift. ([[def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and-geometric-dirac]], [[def-even-dimensional-spinor-bundle-chirality-and-spin-connection]], [[lem-spinor-and-clifford-associated-bundles-are-well-defined]], [[thm-geometric-clifford-module-dirac-index-formula]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] On a compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold, every real de Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative. De Rham integration identifies wedge products with singular cup products and their oriented evaluation. Thus the real intersection form is represented on harmonic two-forms by $\int_X\alpha\wedge\beta$. ([[thm-hodge-laplacian-kernel-represents-de-rham-and-dolbeault-cohomology]], [[thm-de-rham-theorem]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] With the library's connection convention, $c(\nabla)=\det(I-F/(2\pi i))$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\nabla)=\operatorname{tr}\exp(-F/(2\pi i))$. The second Chern form represents the topological second Chern class over the reals. Integration of an exact form on closed $X$ is zero. ([[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], [[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]], [[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The actual smooth-ball small-curvature theorem constructs Euclidean Coulomb gauges with $\|a\|_4+\|a\|_{W^{1,2}}\le C\|F\|_2$ on a unit ball. It applies to arbitrary smooth connections, with exact unitary curvature covariance. ([[lem-small-critical-curvature-coulomb-gauges-on-four-balls]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For a smooth metric sufficiently $C^0$ close to Euclidean, the new curved-metric weak Coulomb theorem proves smoothness, uniform interior coefficient bounds for small $L^4$ potential, and the actual estimate $r^2\|F\|_\infty\le C\|F\|_2$. Its constants are uniform on the rescalings of finitely many fixed compact coordinate charts. It covers either Hodge sign. ([[lem-weak-coulomb-asd-connections-for-smooth-four-metrics-are-interior-smooth]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The annular transport proof gives a frame bounded by the uniform annular curvature, using two spherical path families and quaternionic normalization. The punctured critical-gauge proof aligns adjacent frames by constants and sums a dyadic annular $L^4$ bound. The point-removal proof retains the full quadratic cutoff curvature and constructs a limiting gauge after Coulomb extraction. Their Euclidean-ASD Statements are NOT invoked for a curved metric: the required extensions of these actual arguments are supplied below with [F2]. ([[lem-small-uniform-curvature-gauges-on-four-dimensional-annuli]], [[lem-finite-energy-punctured-euclidean-asd-connections-have-l-four-gauges]], [[lem-finite-energy-euclidean-asd-point-singularity-is-removable]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Close $SU(2)$ cocycles are intertwined by the explicitly proved normalized quaternionic average. Its finite algebra works on any finite chart cover with compactly supported smooth scalar weights; below it is written again for the present smooth data. A countable smooth matrix cocycle glues a smooth vector bundle. For $SU(2)$ transitions its preserved metric, complex structure and determinant give the corresponding principal $SU(2)$ frame bundle. ([[lem-close-su-two-cocycles-admit-constructed-sobolev-isomorphisms]], [[thm-vector-bundle-construction-from-a-smooth-cocycle]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The second Chern form is $c_2(A)=\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A)/(8\pi^2)$ for the trace-zero rank-two connection and represents the integral topological class over the reals. Closed exact top forms integrate to zero. On a coordinate ball, the divergence theorem gives zero integral for the derivative of a smooth three-form with zero tangential boundary trace. Thus, for the sign $F_A^-=0$, $\int|F_A|^2=-8\pi^2\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. These signs follow from the given Frobenius norm and the stated determinant normalization. ([[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]], [[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], [[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]], [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]])

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Arzela–Ascoli, smooth cutoffs, Holder and absolute continuity hold in the stated finite-dimensional smooth charts. Countable diagonal extractions and choices are permitted by full AC. ([[cor-arzela-ascoli-subsequence-theorem-for-proper-metric-targets]], [[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], [[thm-absolute-continuity-of-the-integral]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]])

facts.label: F6

facts.label: F7

facts.label: F8
facts.text: [F8] For any abelian group $A$, $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ is its positive-integer localization, and $a\otimes1=0$ exactly when some positive integer kills $a$. facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Right modules are unital additive groups with the right distributivity and associativity axioms; division rings are unital rings in which every nonzero element is invertible ([[def-ring]], [[def-division-ring]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A balanced biadditive map from a right module and a left module satisfies $b(mr,k)=b(m,rk)$. The tensor product is the free abelian group on pairs modulo these additivity and balancing relations, and its elements are finite sums of elementary tensors ([[def-balanced-and-bilinear-maps]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Exactness means image equals kernel; a left module is flat when tensoring it with right modules is exact, and the right-flat definition has the sides reversed ([[def-exact-and-short-exact-sequences-of-modules]], [[def-left-and-right-flat-modules-over-an-arbitrary-ring]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Tensoring a chain complex means tensoring its terms and differentials, and homology is cycles modulo boundaries ([[def-chain-complex-with-coefficients-by-tensoring]], [[def-homology-object-of-a-chain-complex]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Opposite multiplication reverses factors while leaving addition and identity unchanged ([[def-opposite-ring]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] **Compact finite-input convention.** The classical external results are initially used in ordinary ZFC, not assumed choice-free from their citations. For this one application take finitely many charts covering the given compact manifolds and finitely many pair charts covering each given compact disk or annulus, shrinking to closed inner charts inside open outer charts. Such finite subcovers exist by compactness; selecting this finite list uses no axiom of choice. Include the actual boundary/product collars and all supplied homeomorphisms in the list. Encode chart domains and overlaps by their rational balls, continuous maps and their inverses by dense rational data with moduli on the closed inner charts, and smooth maps by all finite-order derivative and Taylor-remainder data. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. The external relative-constructibility input is that $L[r]$ is an inner model of ZFC containing $r$ (Karagila, §8.3, p.42); no ambient choice hypothesis is required. All compact maps are decoded using these same moduli, so the inverse identities, covers, pair sections and collar equalities are checked on dense rational sets with their displayed buffers and remain valid in the ambient universe $V$. An internally produced compact witness is exported with the same certificates, and hence is an actual ambient compact witness. This uses the peer-checked compact annulus coding pattern of the standard connected-sum compatibility supplier only at its geometric scope; it does not assert that arbitrary homology or fundamental-group hypotheses are absolute.

facts.text: [A1] Full AC is the chosen integral half-solution and analytic convention; it implies the countable-choice hypotheses of the smooth concordance constructions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The actual exterior-to-zero-surgery comparison preserves the integral classical Alexander module and its Blanchfield self-values. [[thm-zero-surgery-identifies-exterior-classical-alexander-and-blanchfield-data]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] In the smooth category, actual integral solution sets are nested subgroups, satellite maps preserve concordance, and every next-iterate image lies in the corresponding integral filtration subgroup plus the cyclic class of the iterate of the unknot. The full proof supplies integral0-solutions, an actual annulus tube with zero boundary framings, homology cobordisms and deep-axis infection solutions. [[thm-smooth-integral-filtration-is-compatible-with-deep-axis-infection]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The full finite-prime smooth obstruction theorem excludes every nonzero signed sum of each chosen finite family of $P^n$ iterates from integral $(n+1/2)$-solvability for $n\ge1$, and supplies a separate actual smooth nonslice nonhomomorphism witness. The finite-cyclic half-solution theorem supplies the actual $n=0$ obstruction. [[thm-finite-prime-smooth-infection-obstructions-use-actual-coefficients]], [[thm-finite-cyclic-extensions-over-integral-half-solutions-have-zero-defect]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The complete smooth all-iterate theorem assembles [F2]–[F3], including finite-cyclic connected-sum additivity, the $n=0$ case, rational independence modulo integral filtrations, the at-most-one cyclic rank loss and the separate nonhomomorphism conclusion. [[thm-smooth-winding-zero-iterates-have-infinite-rank-in-every-quotient]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For supplied initial TOP integral-pair data and the actual finite standard pieces, the Blanchfield-bordism and full-forest meridian calculations hold. Actual finite-projective TOP duality/gluing and the lifted-half-pair vanishing theorem also hold, without smoothing that initial manifold. [[lem-cha-kim-integral-solvability-and-blanchfield-bordism]], [[thm-topological-finite-projective-l2-duality-and-boundary-gluing]], [[thm-topological-lifted-half-pairs-force-amenable-signature-defect-zero]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The finite-stage selection and signed domination argument applies to supplied TOP initial bounds: its actual coefficient maps are supplied by [F5], and its boundary defects agree with the independent smooth invariants by the explicit external closed TOP equality in the rho-independence lemma. [[lem-cha-kim-higher-order-rho-bound-and-coprime-separation]], [[lem-l2-rho-invariant-bordism-independence]], [[thm-cheeger-gromov-uniform-rho-bound]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] An actual TOP integral half-solution with its canonical meridian map to $C_p$ has zero finite-cyclic bounding defect. The exterior/surgery comparison and canonical finite-cyclic signature means use the admitted finite prime signature families. TOP-versus-smooth boundary comparison is supplied by [F6], not assumed in the finite-cyclic theorem. [[thm-finite-cyclic-extensions-over-integral-half-solutions-have-zero-defect]], [[lem-finite-prime-families-have-explicit-separating-knot-signature-bumps]], [[thm-canonical-finite-cyclic-knot-defects-equal-seifert-signature-averages]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] ACω is the countable choice assumption of the regular-projection and smooth isotopy-extension suppliers. [[def-countable-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A regular projection of a smooth knot exists under ACω. It is an immersion with finitely many transverse double points, no triple points, and over/under data specified by strict height inequalities. [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A smooth isotopy of a compact embedded circle in $S^3$ extends to an ambient isotopy under ACω. [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Gluing a ball-arc tangle to its reflected copy, traversed in the opposite direction, gives the oriented connected sum of the tangle's knot closure with its reverse mirror. The connected-sum knot type is independent of the small trivial closing arc. [[def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot]], [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The ribbon condition requires finitely many disjoint transverse double arcs with one proper preimage arc and one interior preimage arc, and no other multiple points. [[def-ribbon-disk-and-ribbon-knot]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] ACω is the assumption used by smooth isotopy extension, parametric transversality, and the Morse-handle suppliers. [[def-countable-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A ribbon immersion has finitely many double arcs with disjoint proper and interior preimage arcs and no other multiple points. A band move is prescribed by a framed embedded rectangle meeting the boundary link only along its two attaching edges. [[def-ribbon-disk-and-ribbon-knot]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A compact collared Morse surface has a finite handle presentation; minima add disks and index-one points add rectangles along opposite edges. At regular intervals, normalized gradient flow identifies the boundary circles. Conversely the standard disk and rectangle handle models have one minimum or one saddle, respectively, and glue along regular collars. [[thm-morse-functions-and-handle-decompositions-correspond]], [[cor-a-morse-function-on-a-compact-manifold-has-finitely-many-critical-points]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A smooth isotopy of a compact boundary link extends ambiently in $S^3$. [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A smooth arc may be perturbed relative to its endpoint collars to be transverse to finitely many immersed surface sheets and disjoint from finitely many immersed arcs in a three-manifold. The first condition has zero-dimensional inverse image and the second has empty inverse image; finite-dimensional bump families and parametric transversality give both simultaneously. [[thm-parametric-transversality]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Under ACω, every smooth oriented knot $K$ has $K\#K^\dagger$ bounding a ribbon immersion in $S^3$, and separately bounding a smooth proper disk whose squared radial function is Morse with only index-$0$ and index-$1$ critical points. facts.label: F6

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The reverse mirror is reflection of the knot followed by reversal of its knot orientation, and the connected sum uses the fixed orientation-matching gluing convention. ([[def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot]], [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A Fox 3-coloring assigns an element of $\mathbb F_3$ to each diagram arc and satisfies $2x_o=x_i+x_j$ at every crossing. ([[def-quandle-and-knot-coloring]], [[lem-dihedral-operation-is-a-quandle]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] For $p=3$, the number of Fox $p$-colorings is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented Reidemeister move. ([[lem-dihedral-fox-coloring-count-is-reidemeister-invariant]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Under ACω, two regular diagrams represent the same oriented knot exactly when connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves. ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] In the source crossing chart, the A-smoothing has weight $A$, the B-smoothing has weight $A^{-1}$, and a closed trivial loop has value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The identity $I$ is the vertical through tangle; $e_i$ is the cap on top and cup on bottom, stacking removes loops with coefficient $\delta$, and the stacking product is associative and bilinear ([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], [[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The generators satisfy $e_i^2=\delta e_i$, $e_ie_{i+1}e_i=e_i$, $e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}=e_{i+1}$, and distant generators commute ([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] R2 creates or deletes two opposite crossings, and every allowed R3 has a strict height order with the cyclic over/under pattern excluded ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] In the positively oriented chart with over-strand southwest–northeast,
the A-smoothing pairs left endpoints and right endpoints, while the B-smoothing
pairs top endpoints and bottom endpoints. A crossing contributes $A$ for its
A-smoothing and $A^{-1}$ for its B-smoothing; a state with $k$ circles contributes the factor
$\delta^{k-1}$, and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$
([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The total writhe is the sum of the signs
$\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$;
the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] A type-I kink creates or deletes one crossing of either sign; type II
creates or deletes two crossings of opposite signs; type III preserves the
signs of its three crossings ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] The raw bracket is unchanged under every R2 and R3 local replacement
([[lem-kauffman-bracket-r2-r3-identities]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] A crossing in the source chart is the A-smoothing with coefficient $A$
plus the B-smoothing with coefficient $A^{-1}$, and the loop value is
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$
([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The positive geometric half twist has the explicit diamond path with label
$i$ passing below the midpoint and label $i+1$ above it; the reflected path is
its inverse ([[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] $B_n$ is generated by $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{n-1}$ with the Artin
braid and distant-commutation relations, and the closure joins corresponding
top and bottom endpoints with the strand orientations respected
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] The vertical identity diagram has $n$ through strands; $e_i$ has a top
cap and bottom cup at positions $i,i+1$; stacking removes each closed loop
with coefficient $\delta$
([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] The generators satisfy $e_i^2=\delta e_i$,
$e_ie_{i+1}e_i=e_i$, $e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}=e_{i+1}$, and distant commutation
([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] The local crossing operators satisfy R2 cancellation and the R3 braid
identity in the declared source chart
([[lem-kauffman-bracket-r2-r3-identities]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] The unnormalized diagram closure trace is cyclic,
$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$, and
$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)e_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$;
when $\delta$ is a unit, $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$
([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]],
[[lem-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-component-identities]]).

facts.label: F8
facts.text:
[F8] The Hecke tower has quadratic relation
$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, and its Ocneanu trace satisfies the tower restriction,
cyclicity, and $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$
([[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]],
[[thm-the-ocneanu-markov-trace-exists-and-is-unique]]).

facts.label: F9
facts.text:
[F9] The assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto T_i$ is a group homomorphism to Hecke
units, and $T_i^{-1}=v^{-1}T_i+(v^{-1}-1)$
([[lem-the-hecke-generators-satisfy-the-artin-relations-and-are-units]]).

facts.label: F10
facts.text:
[F10] The Hecke tower has the decomposition
$H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus H(n)T_nH(n)$ as an $H(n)$-bimodule
([[lem-the-hecke-tower-is-free-over-the-previous-level]]).

facts.label: F11
facts.text:
[F11] The exponent sum is a homomorphism $e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ with
$e(\sigma_i)=1$ ([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$

facts.label: F1

[F1] The normalized bracket is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented
R1, R2, or R3 move ([[lem-kauffman-bracket-curl-and-writhe-correction]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two ambient-isotopic regular oriented link
diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] Every oriented link may be moved off the point at infinity into $\mathbb R^3$,
and the directions giving regular projections are dense in $S^2$
([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]],
[[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]).

facts.text:
[A1] Full AC means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] Full AC implies countable choice
([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The positive Artin half twist has determinant crossing sign $+1$; the
opposite reflected half twist exchanges over and under and has sign $-1$
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] The braid exponent sum is additive, with $e(\sigma_i)=1$ and
$e(\sigma_i^{-1})=-1$
([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] For every braid closure, the normalized bracket satisfies
$$f_{\widehat\beta}(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(\widehat\beta)} \langle\widehat\beta\rangle,$$
and its value is independent of the regular diagram under AC$ _\omega$
([[thm-normalized-bracket-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] For every $n$-braid, the raw bracket has the trace expression
$$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta)) \big|_{v=A^{-4},\,z=-1/(A^{-4}+1)},\qquad \delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$$
([[lem-hecke-bracket-trace-dictionary-and-local-descent]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] The library Jones value is invariant under braid equivalence and Markov
moves under full AC, and is given by the trace formula in the Statement
([[thm-the-hecke-trace-construction-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]],
[[def-temperley-lieb-quotient-and-jones-specialization]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] Every nonempty oriented link has a braid closure under full AC
([[thm-alexanders-closed-braid-theorem]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

facts.label: F8
facts.text:
[F8] Every element of $B_n$ is represented by a finite word in the Artin
generators and their inverses; each letter is one geometric half twist or its
opposite, and the closure joins the braid endpoints
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

facts.text:
[F1] A crossing-free one-component diagram has one state with one circle and
bracket $(-A^2-A^{-2})^{1-1}=1$
([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F2

[F2] Adding a positive type-I kink multiplies the raw bracket by $-A^3$
([[lem-kauffman-bracket-curl-and-writhe-correction]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] An oriented type-I kink is an allowed local Reidemeister replacement and
each such local replacement is realized by an ambient isotopy of the oriented
link ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]],

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] The algorithm enumerates every smoothing state once and adds
$A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}$, with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$
([[alg-kauffman-bracket-state-sum]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] In the declared chart, a positive braid crossing has operator
$C_1=AI+A^{-1}e_1$, with $I$ the two through strands and $e_1$ the top-cap,
bottom-cup diagram ([[lem-hecke-bracket-trace-dictionary-and-local-descent]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] The Temperley–Lieb closure trace assigns $\delta^{c(D)}$ to a basis
diagram, where $c(D)$ counts circles after joining corresponding top and
bottom endpoints. The closure of $I$ has two circles, and the closure of
$e_1$ has one ([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] Stacking satisfies $e_1^2=\delta e_1$
([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] Each positive Artin half twist has crossing sign $+1$; mirroring swaps
over and under and negates the determinant sign
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] The normalized bracket of every nonempty oriented link equals the
library Jones specialization after $t=A^{-4}$
([[thm-bracket-state-sum-matches-library-jones-specialization]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] The closure of the identity one-strand braid is the crossing-free
one-component unknot ([[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

facts.text:
[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written AC$_\omega$

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] The Dubrovnik scalar $P$ is regular-isotopy invariant, has $P(\varnothing)=1$,
positive/negative curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, loop factor $d$, and skein
$P_+-P_-=z(P_0-P_\infty)$ over $z(d-1)=a-a^{-1}$
([[lem-framed-kauffman-link-evaluation]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The determinant writhe is the signed sum of crossing signs; reversing one
strand negates that crossing sign, while reversing both strands preserves it
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] The mixed crossing sum between two distinct oriented components is even
([[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] A type-I move changes one self-crossing, type II adds or removes two
opposite-sign crossings, and type III preserves its three crossing signs
([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] In the stated polynomial convention, $D=P/d$ on nonempty diagrams,
$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ)$, and $F=A^{-w}L$
([[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions]]).

[F1] The BMW relation is $g_i-g_i^{-1}=z_B(1-e_i)$, the coefficient relation is

$g_ie_i=e_ig_i=\rho^{-1}e_i$, $e_ig_{i\pm1}e_i=\rho e_i$, and

facts.label: F2

facts.label: F3

the top/bottom pairing as the B-smoothing for an over-strand directed
southwest to northeast ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F4] The coefficient extension is $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$, with
$z_B=q-q^{-1}$, $z_D=z_B$, $\rho=a$, and $\delta=d$
([[def-bmw-dubrovnik-coefficient-extension]]).

facts.text: [F5] R1, R2, and R3 are the local kink, two-strand cancellation, and strand-past-crossing replacements, with all sign and orientation variants; planar isotopy transports the diagram without creating or deleting a crossing ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]], [[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]).

facts.text: [A2] Countable choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, means every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A diffeomorphism induces a skein-module isomorphism by transporting framed links, and a matching product collar carries the closed-link action by gluing and disjoint union; this action is natural under collar-preserving diffeomorphisms ([[lem-general-3manifold-skein-quotient-isotopy-and-gluing]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A positive or negative full framing twist on one component multiplies its skein class by $-A^3$ or $-A^{-3}$ ([[lem-kauffman-bracket-module-framing-twist-factor]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The empty class is a free $R$-basis of $\mathcal K_A(S^3)$ and a zero-framed trivial circle has class $\delta[\varnothing]$ ([[thm-skein-module-of-s-three-is-rank-one]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The blackboard-framed core classes $[z^n]$, $n\geq0$, are an $R$-basis of the solid-torus module ([[thm-skein-module-of-solid-torus-has-core-multicurve-basis]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Here $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ is the Laurent-polynomial ring over the integral domain $\mathbb Z$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ has basis $1,X$, with $m(1\otimes1)=1$, $m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X$, $m(X\otimes X)=0$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, and $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$; the maps satisfy associativity, coassociativity and the Frobenius identities ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] For a based knot, the quotient removes the based-circle $X$ label and is identified statewise with the interval module $M=\mathbb Z$, $X\cdot1=0$. facts.label: F5

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] For the actual balanced $S^3$ diagram, the full-marked count theorem constructs ONE integrable background and genuine time-collar path with marked positivity, no nonconstant strip of index at most zero, regularity of every actual index-one and index-two strip, and finitely many rigid translation orbits across ALL generators/classes/nonnegative marked degrees. It also supplies finite regular endpoint unit disks: their parities are one for every alpha and beta cut component if $k\ge2$, and zero for both components if $k=1$, with actual pointed sphere avoidance in that latter case. All positive $z$ multiplicities are included. ([[thm-balanced-knot-data-admit-full-marked-square-zero-holomorphic-counts]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For THE path constructed in [F1], the full-marked compactification theorem gives an actual compact one-manifold for each pair of generators and pair of nonnegative marked vectors. Its finite boundary consists EXACTLY of broken rigid pairs and the unit boundary disks attached to a constant generator. All have actual exhaustive one-sided gluing collars. Its proof first uses actual bounded-energy bubble extraction and index additivity and then the nonpositive-index exclusion to check limiting-strip regularity; it excludes the singly pointed sphere alternative by the actual sphere avoidance. ([[thm-full-marked-index-two-compactification-gives-the-boundary-disk-curvature-identity]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Actual unbubbled strip neck cutoffs and regular gluing preserve Whitney concatenation. The actual boundary-disk attachment theorem constructs corrected maps in the class of the source plumbing, with exhaustive collars. Boundary-preserving local addition gives actual relative homotopies between sufficiently close compact cores. ([[lem-unbubbled-strip-breaking-and-regular-gluing-preserve-whitney-concatenation]], [[thm-regular-boundary-disk-attachment-has-an-exhaustive-nodal-half-collar]], [[lem-boundary-preserving-local-addition-for-transverse-product-tori]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The actual relative Alexander grading satisfies $A(x)-A(y)=\sum_i n_{z_i}(u)-\sum_i n_{w_i}(u)$ for every realized Whitney class; each $U_i$ lowers filtration by one. The original full minus differential counts every $z$ degree with weight $U^{n_w}$. ([[thm-balanced-s-three-knot-generators-admit-consistent-relative-gradings]], [[def-admissible-pointed-heegaard-floer-data]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The grid grading formulas are integral, and every realized flat-grid Whitney class satisfies the full relative Maslov and Alexander formulas, including positive X multiplicity. Its index is $n_x(D)+n_y(D)$, and its local domain equation is $\Delta D=1_x-1_y$. Actual integrable full disk counts are precisely the finitely many regular empty-state rectangles, with all individual O weights. ([[lem-grid-alexander-grading-integral]], [[thm-realized-grid-whitney-classes-have-the-full-relative-grading-formula]], [[lem-realized-flat-grid-index-one-positive-domains-are-empty-rectangles]], [[thm-integrable-flat-grid-rectangle-counts-equal-the-full-filtered-grid-differential]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The purely combinatorial grid maps and inverse homotopies preserve the stated J-formula Maslov grading and Alexander filtration. Commutation preserves tilde homology; stabilization adds the zero-differential factor V of degrees (0,0),(-1,-1). Over one chosen variable action they are actual filtered equivalences with independent variables retained. Grid moves generate oriented knot isotopy. These results concern finite grid domains and do not invoke the grid-to-analytic identification proved here. ([[thm-grid-commutation-stabilization-invariance-proof]], [[thm-grid-moves-generate-oriented-knot-isotopy]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The analytic full-minus auxiliary comparisons apply to any finite square-zero count endpoints with no nonconstant nonpositive-index strips and regular index-one strips. The actual balanced-knot diagram comparison, ordinary target-neck stabilization and marked-pair cone then give equivalence over one chosen action with a normalized doubly pointed complex. Ordinary collapse instead gives its tensor product with V to the number of extra pairs. All these comparisons retain positive z terms. The multipointed relative origins are fixed by transport from the doubly pointed Seifert-Chern and total-hat normalizations, with source cone shift (-1,-1). ([[thm-balanced-knot-full-minus-auxiliary-continuations-are-filtered-equivalences]], [[thm-pointed-heegaard-floer-invariance-under-moves-and-stabilization]], [[lem-pointed-basepoint-cone-and-variable-collapse]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The normalized doubly pointed total zero-w hat homology is one-dimensional in Maslov degree zero. Analytic conjugation identifies its Alexander-associated-graded homology in degrees (m,a) and (m-2a,-a), independently of any grid comparison. Its Alexander origin is the negative modified-Morse field with zero-relative-Euler Seifert cap, hence the stated half-Chern pairing. ([[lem-relative-s-three-maslov-gradings-have-a-unique-hat-homology-normalization]], [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]], [[lem-doubly-pointed-knot-morse-fields-have-a-zero-framed-seifert-extension]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The grid is admissible. The grid algorithm's full and associated-graded rectangle matrices square to zero and have the stated variable actions. ([[lem-grid-diagram-is-admissible]], [[lem-grid-rectangle-differential-squares-to-zero]], [[alg-grid-knot-floer-complex]])
