facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] **External construction input.** Zemke, *Link cobordisms and functoriality in link Floer homology*, arXiv:1610.05207v3, Theorem A (p.3), Definitions 2.1–2.4 (pp.7–8), Proposition 3.5 and §3.4 (p.14), and §12 (pp.85–97), constructs the fixed-Spin-c colored maps for the full decorated category, as filtered equivariant chain maps on transitive chain homotopy types. Boundary parametrizations are retained (Remark 2.6, p.8). Components need not meet both ends: §12.5, Definition 12.8, Lemma 12.9 and equation (55) (pp.95–97) supply puncturing and the 0/4-handle maps. This is an explicitly imported established theorem, not a reconstruction from the local triangle lemma. ([Source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] **External elementary-input convention.** For a two-handle use the standard auxiliary top homology class in Zemke §5. For band surgery the actual inputs are the classes $\Theta^w$ for a type-z band and $\Theta^z$ for a type-w band (§§6.2–6.3, pp.46–47; auxiliary unlink calculation Lemmas 3.7 and 6.4). Choose cycle representatives. Changing a representative by a boundary changes the triangle map by filtered equivariant chain homotopy (§6.2, p.46). There is no canonical chain generator on arbitrary triples. The displayed formula is the beta-triple convention; alpha-triples insert the auxiliary cycle in the other tensor factor. The dividing set chooses the band type. ([Source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] **Two-color scope.** Color every component of $\Sigma_w$ by $U$ and every component of $\Sigma_z$ by $V$. This is a coloring in Definition 2.3 and induces exactly the given endpoint coloring. Remark 2.14 (p.10) gives zero curvature for this specialization, including intermediate links; §3.4 gives the colored polynomial modules and variable-power filtration.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **Countable-choice specialization of the imported construction.** Use the retained Countable-Choice theorem on full-marked low-dimensional polygons at its stated coherent-relative-face scope, with finite balanced diagrams, fixed labels and all nonnegative marked multiplicities. It supplies regular perturbations, finite counts, compact one-manifolds and gluing for the disk/polygon boundary identities used here. Its permitted small pointed curve choices retain the Spin-c labels and admissibility. The general naturality/move identities, top-input calculations and geometric decomposition theorems remain the explicitly external parts of [F1]–[F2], not conclusions of polygon analysis alone. Their remaining choices are finite topological data and countably indexed analytic families for each specified input/comparison, as detailed below. ([[thm-strictly-admissible-triple-free-polygons-have-full-marked-low-dimensional-counts]], [[lem-knot-floer-holomorphic-triangle-transversality-compactness-gluing]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] **External full naturality theorem.** Zemke, arXiv:1610.05207v3, Theorem A (p.3), gives a fixed-Spin-c $\mathbb Z^P$-filtered $\mathbb F_2[X_p:p\in P]$-equivariant chain map, invariant under diffeomorphism up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. Diagram changes are compared by the transitive system of Definition 2.15 and Proposition 3.5 (§§2.2 and 3.3, pp.11–14). Theorem 11.5 and its proof (pp.74 and 84–85), followed by Theorem A' and its fourteen-move proof (§12.4, pp.91–95), supply changes of parametrized Kirby decomposition. Definition 12.8, Lemma 12.9 and the final proof of Theorem A (§12.5, pp.95–97) supply empty-end puncturing and its independence. These are imported results; their move checks are not claimed as locally reconstructed. ([Source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] **External Spin-c composition theorem.** Zemke, Theorem B (pp.3 and 97–98), gives the exact extension-sum formula in the Statement. Its proof stacks decompositions, reorders the elementary maps, applies the two-handle composition law (Proposition 5.10, p.43), and handles empty ends by puncturing. facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Actual admissible doubly pointed S3 diagrams have the full filtered minus count complex, retaining positive multiplicities at BOTH marks. The differential counts actual index-one classes with coefficient $U^{n_w}$; its degree is minus one. The accepted analytic construction supplies finite counts and square zero. [[def-admissible-pointed-heegaard-floer-data]] [[lem-heegaard-floer-holomorphic-disk-regularity-compactness-gluing]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Every two generators of a balanced S3 diagram are joined by an actual Whitney class, and the integer relative gradings satisfy $M(x)-M(y)=\mu(\phi)-2n_w(\phi)$ and $A(x)-A(y)=n_z(\phi)-n_w(\phi)$. The Seifert normalization is the actual NEGATIVE modified Morse field with its zero-relative-Euler cap; it is carried by oriented diagram data. Total zero-w hat homology is one-dimensional and its sole class has normalized Maslov degree zero. [[thm-balanced-s-three-knot-generators-admit-consistent-relative-gradings]] [[lem-doubly-pointed-knot-morse-fields-have-a-zero-framed-seifert-extension]] [[lem-relative-s-three-maslov-gradings-have-a-unique-hat-homology-normalization]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Between actual doubly pointed diagrams of the SAME oriented knot in S3 there are full minus filtered equivalences with filtered inverse homotopies, preserving the absolute Seifert origin and normalized Maslov degree. Every term $U^a y$ has $a\ge0$ and $A(y)-a\le A(x)$; thus localization is nonincreasing in both bifiltration coordinates. [[thm-doubly-pointed-s-three-moves-preserve-the-seifert-normalized-filtration]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The accepted real-operator conjugation uses the coefficientwise conjugation map $C:\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma,j)\to\operatorname{Sym}^g(-\Sigma,-j)$, defined in symmetric root-coordinate charts and smooth even at collisions. Conjugating target and source and interchanging the two boundary labels gives literal operator and divisor-degree correspondence, with all marked weights retained. The explicit calculation is also repeated below for the two needed strip maps. [[thm-balanced-knot-attaching-moves-have-full-minus-inverse-maps]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Reversing the ambient orientation and the knot orientation is exactly the reverse-mirror convention in the Statement. [[def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The resolved signed top/outer comparison in [[lem-ni-holomorphic-disk-and-jsj-analytic-inputs]] identifies the actual grading-$g$ complex with the actual $F$-cut complex, with its induced coherent orientation class. Thus it identifies their integral homologies. This is also the exact external Theorem 1.5 of Juhász, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, published p.300, for a null-homologous knot in any closed connected oriented $Y$ and any Seifert surface $F$; no three-sphere or rational-homology-sphere hypothesis occurs.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] **External vanishing input:** Juhász, *Holomorphic discs and sutured manifolds*, Proposition 9.18, published pp.1452–1453: if a balanced sutured manifold is irreducible and not taut, its integral sutured Floer homology is zero. This is used by contrapositive, independently of the resolved taut-to-nonzero hierarchy theorem.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] **External nonproduct input:** Juhász, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, Theorem 9.7, published pp.343–348: every taut balanced sutured manifold which is not a product has integral sutured Floer homology containing a copy of $\mathbb Z^2$. Its geometric reduction, including the characteristic-pair step, is an external input here, not a locally reconstructed consequence of the $S^3$ JSJ theorem. The source's proof reduces by horizontal/product-annulus operations and produces two taut decompositions with disjoint outer $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ sets. Their nonzero summands and signed cut maps agree with the scopes of the preserved local hierarchy and analytic suppliers. In particular no integral homology tensor formula without Tor is assumed.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **Corrected external characteristic-pair input:** the original Ni characteristic-product-region citation is not imported uncorrected. Ni's Corrigendum, author-version pp.1–3, Theorem 4 and Definitions 5–6, uses a characteristic Seifert pair for a Haken manifold pair and a maximal gapless product pair containing its characteristic product pair. Theorem 6.2-prime assumes irreducible balanced, connected suture, vertically prime, and $\widehat{\mathrm{HFS}}\cong\mathbb Z$; it says that product-annulus homologies span $H_1(M)$. Corollary 7 says that the characteristic product pair then surjects onto $H_1(M)$. The corrected main proof on p.3 supplies the product reduction in the original arbitrary-$Y$ setting. These are source qualifications for the external product argument in F3 and Ni's Theorem 1.1, not assertions of the false universal ambient enclosure used in the uncorrected paper. None is deduced from the retained $S^3$ knot-exterior JSJ Statement.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Riesz transforms are the $L^2$ Fourier multipliers $-i\xi_j/|\xi|$ and are bounded on every $L^p$, $1<p<\infty$ ([[def-riesz-transforms-on-euclidean-space]], [[cor-riesz-transforms-are-bounded-on-lp]]). Fourier differentiation and Plancherel agreement and injectivity justify multiplier identities for smooth compactly supported functions ([[thm-fourier-differentiation-and-multiplication-identities-on-tempered-distributions]], [[thm-fourier-transform-agrees-with-l-one-and-plancherel-transforms]], [[thm-plancherel]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Smooth Sobolev approximation and the weak smooth-factor product rule hold; smooth cutoffs between balls exist. Multiplying global smooth approximants by a fixed cutoff gives compactly supported smooth approximants to a compactly supported Sobolev class ([[thm-meyers-serrin-density-on-an-arbitrary-open-set]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]], [[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A $W^{1,p}$-bounded sequence on a bounded smooth ball has an $L^p$-convergent subsequence. Balls are extension domains, and for $2\le p<4$, $W^{1,p}(B_1)\hookrightarrow L^{4p/(4-p)}(B_1)$ continuously ([[thm-rellich-compactness-from-w-one-p-to-lp-on-an-extension-domain]], [[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]], [[thm-sobolev-embedding-on-bounded-extension-domains-for-p-less-than-n]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Distributionally harmonic locally integrable functions are smooth. The mean-zero Poincare inequality holds on $B_1$ and its rescaled balls ([[cor-locally-integrable-weakly-harmonic-functions-are-smooth]], [[lem-mean-zero-poincare-estimate-on-bounded-connected-extension-domains-for-p-less-than-n]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Holder, $L^p$ completeness and monotone convergence are available. Divergence gives integration by parts for smooth forms on the closed ball; [F2] and the extension theorem in [F3] give density of functions smooth near the closed ball in $W^{1,2}(B_1)$ ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]], [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]).

facts.text: [F1] **External admissible closure input.** Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Knots, sutures and excision*, arXiv:0807.4891v2, §7.1 and Definition 7.3, supplies the ordinary instanton group for a fixed determinant line bundle with odd pairing on an integral surface and the commuting point/surface operators. The auxiliary surface has a closed curve whose two boundary-surface copies are nonseparating; in this annular knot construction its core has that property. facts.label: F2

The source uses complex coefficients for convenience. The rational version used here is explicitly permitted in Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector*, §1.1, PDF p. 3, immediately before Proposition 1.4.

facts.text: [F1] On $B_1$ the constructed normal-boundary Hodge estimate applies to the closure classes $Y_p$ and, for $p=2,3$, absorbs the curvature nonlinearity when $\|a\|_4\le\rho_p$. It then bounds $\|a\|_{W^{1,p}}$ by $C_p\|F_a\|_p$ for Coulomb forms ([[lem-normal-boundary-hodge-estimate-on-four-dimensional-balls]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For $a\in Y_3$ Coulomb with $\|a\|_4\le\rho_c$, and $\lambda\in Y_3$ with sufficiently small $W^{1,3}$ norm, the proved contraction constructs a Neumann gauge $h=e^u$ with $b=(a+\lambda)^h\in Y_3$ Coulomb, and $\|b-a\|_{W^{1,3}}\le C_c(1+\|a\|_{W^{1,3}})\|\lambda\|_{W^{1,3}}$. It preserves given finite constant-conjugation equivariance. Its Neumann gauge class is the $W^{2,3}$ closure $\mathcal G_N$ of smooth $SU(2)$ maps with zero normal derivative ([[lem-neumann-coulomb-gauge-correction-by-contraction]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] **External ordinary determinant-$w$ surface input.** For a closed oriented three-manifold $Y$ and a Hermitian line bundle $w$ with odd pairing on an integral surface class, use the determinant-one gauge group of a $U(2)$ lift with fixed determinant $w$. Its admissible instanton homology and commuting operators $\mu(R),\mu(y)$ are defined. For $S^1\times R$, $g(R)\ge1$, with $c_1(w)$ dual to $S^1$, the ordinary-$w$ product calculation has the spectrum in Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Knots, sutures and excision*, Proposition 7.1; the common extreme eigenspace $I_*(S^1\times R\mid R)_w$ is one-dimensional by Proposition 7.4. On the point-$+2$ kernel the extreme surface factor is simple, as stated immediately after Proposition 7.4. Corollary 7.2 and Proposition 7.5 give the surface bounds on a general admissible $Y$, including the case where $w$ pairs evenly with the other surface; Corollary 7.6 gives the simultaneous generalized-eigenspace decomposition. These are imported published all-genus ordinary-$w$ results, not consequences inferred here from an altered $u$ or $uw$ module. Locators: arXiv:0807.4891v2, §§7.1–7.2, PDF pp. 52–56.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **External excision and closure input.** Theorem 7.7 of the same source gives excision for two oriented embedded positive-equal-genus surfaces, with equal odd $c_1(w)$ evaluations, an orientation-compatible gluing diffeomorphism and its chosen determinant-bundle lift; when $Y$ is connected the two surfaces are required not to be homologous, and for two components one lies in each. The disconnected group is interpreted as a tensor product. Definition 7.10 and the closure-independence argument following it establish that the sutured group is independent, up to isomorphism, of the allowed auxiliary surface and marked gluing choices. The closure has $c_1(w)$ dual to the standard circle through the fixed auxiliary point. Genus one is permitted. In the meridional knot case Definition 7.13 identifies the annular-auxiliary closure with the torus closure; its group is precisely the simultaneous $(\mu(\bar R),\mu(y))=(0,2)$ eigenspace, equivalently the point-$+2$ half, not the doubled full Floer group. Locators: arXiv:0807.4891v2, Theorem 7.7, Definition 7.10 and its following argument, Definition 7.13, PDF pp. 56–61. The source works over $\mathbb C$ for convenience; the rational version is explicitly allowed in the detector paper's §1.1, PDF p. 3.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] **External decomposition, nonvanishing and genus/rank input.** For a balanced sutured manifold decomposed along a surface $S$ with no closed components, and with the closed components of $S\cap V$ parallel oriented boundary-coherent simple closed curves for each component $V$ of $R(\gamma)$, Proposition 7.11 gives the decomposed sutured instanton group as a direct summand (the precise hypotheses of Theorem 6.8, PDF p. 48); Theorem 7.12 states that a taut balanced sutured manifold has nonzero sutured instanton homology. For a classical genus-$g$ knot, Proposition 7.16 gives $KHI(K,g)\ne0$, with the genus decomposition and its opposite extreme as in §7.6. In particular a nontrivial classical knot has $\dim KHI(K)>1$. Locators: arXiv:0807.4891v2, §§7.5–7.6, PDF pp. 59–64, and Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector*, §1.1, PDF p. 3, which explicitly records this rank consequence and permits $\mathbb Q$ coefficients. These decomposition/nonvanishing conclusions are imported established results; no local cap/module or taut-hierarchy proof is asserted here.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] **External rational singular-to-sutured bridge.** For a based smooth knot in $S^3$, Proposition 1.4 of *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector* states $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Q)\cong KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$. Its §5.4, Proposition 5.7, uses the actual earring link $K\cup L$ and its connecting $w_2$ arc; the two tubular-boundary tori are glued exchanging meridians and longitudes and matching the arc endpoints. The excision has a Hopf-link factor $\mathbb Z$ and the complementary torus closure. The determinant-one group and the larger gauge quotient are distinguished there: the full ordinary knot group has twice the rank, and the point-$+2$ summand is $KHI$. The stated rational bridge includes this normalization. Locators: Proposition 1.4, PDF p. 3, and §5.4, Proposition 5.7 and its following paragraphs, PDF pp. 74–75. No integral bridge or distinguished canonical vector is inferred.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Every prime ideal of height one in a finite-variable polynomial ring over a field is principal and generated by an irreducible element ([[lem-finite-variable-polynomial-rings-over-fields-are-ufds]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For an affine domain of finite type over a field, its Krull dimension is the transcendence degree of its fraction field ([[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Geometric dimension of an affine algebraic set over an algebraically closed field equals Krull dimension of its coordinate ring, under full AC ([[thm-affine-variety-dimension-coordinate-ring]]; [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The torus is affine: $(M,L)\mapsto(M,L,M^{-1},L^{-1})$ identifies it with $\{(M,L,U,V):MU=LV=1\}\subset\mathbb C^4$.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] For a finite-type domain $A$ and prime $P$, full AC gives $\operatorname{ht}(P)+\dim(A/P)=\dim A$ ([[cor-height-plus-quotient-dimension-affine-domain]]; [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Prime ideals disjoint from a localization set correspond by extension and contraction, preserving inclusions ([[thm-prime-spectrum-of-a-localisation-bijection]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The Laurent polynomial ring is the localization of $\mathbb C[M,L]$ obtained by inverting $M$ and $L$; its units are nonzero scalars times monomials, as follows from polynomial factorization in [F1].

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] The fixed field of all automorphisms of $\mathbb C$ fixing $\mathbb Q$ is $\mathbb Q$ ([[lem-fixed-field-of-automorphisms-of-c-over-q-is-q]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A finite wedge of $n$ circles has fundamental group freely generated by its oriented circle loops; Seifert–van Kampen computes the group of a two-set open cover as the pushout ([[thm-fundamental-group-of-finite-wedge-of-circles]]; [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space has a simply connected universal cover; based maps from a simply connected locally path-connected source lift uniquely after fixing the image of one point ([[thm-universal-cover-existence]]; [[thm-covering-space-lifting-criterion]]). Under the no-reversal deck identification, cover chains are free right group-ring modules on supplied oriented cell lifts, with $c\cdot g=T_{g^{-1}}c$ ([[def-right-group-ring-action-on-the-chains-of-a-universal-cover]]; [[thm-deck-group-of-a-universal-cover-is-the-fundamental-group]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] For a path-connected space, integral $H_1$ is the abelianization of its fundamental group; ordinary cellular chains compute integral singular homology ([[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]; [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]). Free modules are projective under AC ([[thm-free-modules-are-projective-with-choice-boundary]]; [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Augmented projective complexes exact in degrees0/1 have unique comparison isomorphisms on first homology after tensoring with an arbitrary module on the opposite side; no flatness or exactness in degree2 is required ([[lem-partial-projective-resolutions-determine-tensor-homology-in-degree-one]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Intrinsic singular local chains are defined on arbitrary spaces, with coefficients in the fibre at the first vertex and transport on the zeroth face. For connected CW spaces they agree with right-cover-chain tensor left-coefficient-module chains, with $g a=T_{\bar g}a$; cellular comparison is natural, and a based homotopy preserves the induced local homology class with the prescribed coefficient transport ([[def-singular-and-cellular-chain-complexes-with-local-coefficients]]; [[thm-cellular-chains-compute-homology-with-local-coefficients]]; [[prop-local-coefficient-homology-and-cohomology-are-functorial-for-a-map-with-a-coefficient-morphism]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The adjoint torus calculation gives an explicit basis with invariant vector $M-\operatorname{tr}(M)I/2$ when $\operatorname{tr}(M)^2\ne4$, together with a chain contraction of the complementary plane ([[lem-nonparabolic-adjoint-torus-homology-has-explicit-peripheral-basis]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] The actual compact smooth knot exterior is path-connected: the open complement is path-connected by the local Alexander-duality calculation in [[lem-the-complement-of-an-oriented-link-is-a-connected-smooth-three-manifold]], Proof1.3–2.1, and retracts onto the chosen compact exterior by the explicit radial formula in [[lem-maximal-abelian-cover-link-exterior-retraction]], Proof1.1. We use only these proved connectedness/retraction portions; the former carrier's separate quoted finite-triangulation input is not used. Boundary tube charts make the compact exterior a smooth manifold with boundary.

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice assumptions used in the smooth surface and isotopy suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The relative exterior group $H_2(E_K,\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is generated by the oriented fiber, and its intersection-dual meridian class generates $H^1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Geometric incompressibility of a neat two-sided smooth surface is equivalent to fundamental-group injectivity. Broad smooth boundary-preimage surfaces first admit a boundary-fixed embedding neatification, and their actual smooth disk obstructions pass to that representative. [[thm-smooth-loop-theorem-and-incompressibility-criterion-in-orientable-three-manifolds]], [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]], [[lem-angular-boundary-neatification-preserves-smooth-disk-obstructions]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A finite disjoint family of essential longitude curves on a smooth torus admits a simultaneous smooth normalization to the corresponding parallel affine circles. Its isotopy extends into the boundary collar by applying its time parameter times a collar cutoff. [[lem-choice-free-smooth-torus-curves-and-annulus-strips]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] An injective map of compact finite PL oriented surfaces with nontrivial source group is homotopic to a finite covering or to an annular boundary collapse. A boundary local homeomorphism can be fixed throughout. The actual thirteen-row proof gives subgroup cores, the boundary orientation-chain calculation, cutting-arc normalization and disk extension. Smooth compact surfaces have compatible finite cellulations; relative finite simplicial approximation gives the PL map in this interface, preserving an already matched boundary triangulation. [[thm-pi-one-injective-finite-pl-surface-maps-are-covers-or-annular-collapses]], [[lem-compact-c2-surfaces-admit-finite-cellulations-relative-to-a-finite-embedded-graph]], [[thm-finite-simplicial-approximation-for-maps-of-pairs]]

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Connected subgroup covers and their map-lifting criterion exist. Finite surface graph thickenings give the disk conclusion for a simply connected compact surface with nonempty boundary; cellular relative homology computes the orientation-chain degree. [[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]], [[thm-covering-space-lifting-criterion]], [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], [[thm-relative-cellular-homology-computes-relative-singular-homology]]

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The actual boundary-relative homotopic-surface theorem supplies a downstairs embedded family-innermost product patch and the intersection-reducing isotopy. Its proof includes the relative half-product normalization and verifies the boundary-complement injections in the cut fiber product; it does not project an arbitrary cover isotopy. [[thm-boundary-relative-homotopic-incompressible-surfaces-in-fibered-exteriors-are-isotopic]]

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Compact smooth manifolds with corners admit finite compatible triangulations relative to admissible triangulated boundary faces and protected collar neighborhoods. Cutting the smooth pair at its transverse surface faces gives exactly these compatible corner data; paired face subdivisions are matched before regluing. [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]

facts.text: [F1] The boundary inclusion induces restriction on representations; evaluation of each fixed peripheral word is regular in matrix entries because inverse letters in $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ are adjugate polynomials ([[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]]). facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Dehn filling kills the primitive slope $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ and glues a solid torus ([[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Seifert–van Kampen identifies the filled fundamental group with the pushout of the exterior and attached solid-torus groups ([[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]; [[thm-group-pushout-as-an-amalgamated-quotient]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] A deformation retraction induces mutually inverse isomorphisms on fundamental groups at each basepoint of the retract ([[prop-retracts-inject-fundamental-groups]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The fundamental group of the quotient circle is isomorphic to $(\mathbb Z,+)$ by the degree map ([[thm-fundamental-group-of-the-circle]]); the based homeomorphism $[t]\mapsto e^{2\pi i t}$ identifies it with the unit circle.

facts.label: A1

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Under countable choice, a smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar; a collar is a product embedding of the boundary with a half-open interval whose image is a neighbourhood ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]; [[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The exterior is compact orientable and irreducible, with no proper compressing disk. Full AC supplies the countable choice needed by its smooth Schoenflies branch. Its tube is a smooth $S^1\times D^2$ product by the normal-circle frame supplier, so the boundary is the marked smooth torus. It is connected: join two distinct exterior points by an embedded spherical arc, perturb it relative to its endpoints to be transverse to the knot, and use $1+1<3$ to conclude it misses the knot. Radial projection of nonzero tube fibers to their boundary fixes the exterior and retracts that arc to an exterior path; equal endpoints need the constant path. facts.label: F3

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Filling with primitive slope $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ imposes the actual group relation $\mu^p\lambda^q=1$. Abelianization of a knot group is generated by its meridian. A unitary reducible two-dimensional representation is simultaneously diagonal: the orthogonal complement of its invariant line is invariant as well. Consequently its image is abelian, and a representation with abelian image factors through the cyclic abelianization of the filled group. Thus SU2-abelian and SU2-cyclic are equivalent here, including the zero-slope case. [[def-sl-two-abelian-surgery]] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The actual finite representation and common-eigenline incidence varieties have finitely many irreducible components. For each component, dimension of its affine image is the transcendence degree of its coordinate function field. The generic adjoint trace pairing, cap identity, pair exact sequence and word derivations apply over the actual finitely generated characteristic-zero field. [[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]] [[lem-classical-affine-algebraic-set-finite-irreducible-components]] [[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]] [[lem-generic-adjoint-peripheral-kernel-is-the-logarithmic-conormal-line]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The ordinary A-polynomial is a nonzero square-free Laurent equation for the one-dimensional peripheral eigenvalue-image components, including the abelian component. It omits isolated image components but not points on a curve component. [[def-knot-a-polynomial]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The actual marked pattern/companion filling transfers, including reducible nonabelian SL2 cases, and the closed hyperbolic holonomy lift are already supplied. They do not establish the instanton alternative [L1], L-space surgery, or Alexander coefficient restrictions. [[lem-satellite-sl2-abelian-fillings-transfer-to-pattern-and-companion]] [[lem-closed-oriented-hyperbolic-holonomy-has-a-faithful-sl2-lift]]

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] **External input:** Sivek–Zentner, *SU(2)-cyclic surgeries and the pillowcase*, arXiv:1710.01957v2, Theorem 4.1 (statement on pp.3–4 and in §4), proves for EVERY nontrivial knot the following alternative: either the entire vertical circle $\alpha=\pi/2$ is realized by irreducible SU2 representations, or there is an arc of irreducible representations with meridian $\operatorname{diag}(e^{is},e^{-is})$, $s\in[\pi/2,\pi/2+\epsilon)$, $\epsilon>0$. This is imported in its actual varying-meridian scope; neither isolated representation existence nor the local analytic complex is substituted for it.

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] **External inputs:** Baldwin–Sivek, arXiv:2405.19197v2, Theorem 2.7 and Corollary 2.8 (p.6) give boundedness of the FULL SU2-abelian slope set, its unique rational limit $r(K)$ with $|r(K)|>2$, the stated one-sided instanton L-space surgery range, and the knot-or-mirror instanton L-space conclusion. Theorems 2.1–2.2 and Corollary 2.3 (pp.4–5) give fiberedness, alternating nonzero unit Alexander coefficients, and the additional adjacent highest terms $\pm(t^g-t^{g-1}+O(t^{g-2}))$. Lemma 2.4, Proposition 2.16 and Proposition 3.1 give precisely the satellite restrictions with their displayed winding, pattern and companion hypotheses; Lemmas 5.3–5.4 give the filling transfers. The classical knot trichotomy used in their Proposition 2.15 and proofs in §§4–5 is imported at that knot-exterior scope: a nontrivial nontorus nonsatellite knot is hyperbolic. No arbitrary atoroidal manifold assertion is inferred from a definition. These are established external results, not new local proofs of their gauge or hyperbolization foundations.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The signed torus group has central $h=x^a=y^b$ and preferred longitude $\lambda=h\mu^{-ab}$. A knot meridian normally generates its group. Exterior homology is generated by that meridian, with preferred longitude zero. [[thm-torus-knot-group-presentation]] [[lem-satellite-peripheral-representations-transfer-thinness]] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Filling kills precisely the primitive peripheral word. An abelian satellite filling transfers to the same pattern-closure slope and, for signed $w\ne0$, to the companion slope divided by $w^2$, through the actual diagonal, Jordan and central-character-twist constructions. [[def-sl-two-abelian-surgery]] [[lem-satellite-sl2-abelian-fillings-transfer-to-pattern-and-companion]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A supplied complete finite-volume hyperbolic knot metric has complete closed smooth hyperbolic fillings at all but finitely many primitive slopes. The complete metric has a universal $\mathbb H^3$ cover and faithful projective holonomy. For a CLOSED oriented smooth such manifold the actual complete-Heegaard Spin frame cover supplies a faithful SL2 lift. Finite-sheet covers of compact spaces are compact. In an ordinarily weak specified sector the nonnegative domains at each fixed entire mark vector and finite actual index set are finite. Strict admissibility additionally gives a lower strip index and finite domains in every bounded upper-index family; that additional conclusion is not used for the ordinary weak branch. ([[lem-pointed-transverse-multidiagrams-admit-small-triple-free-curve-representatives]], [[lem-heegaard-polygon-spin-c-difference-is-the-capped-periodic-domain]], [[lem-strong-polygon-admissibility-bounds-indices-and-positive-domains]])

facts.text: [F3] On a globally weak multidiagram, coherent source-dependent choices exist with all-index regular zero-marked end strips and polygons, genuine endpoint collars, actual arbitrary product-angle charts, prescribed compatible protected geometry and arbitrarily small perturbations about a compatible reference. The proved finite-count theorem gives stable-source compactness, actual index budgets, exhaustive nonlinear gluing, compact Hausdorff one-manifolds and all zero-marked A-infinity boundaries, including the direct rank-zero model and relative parameter construction. ([[thm-globally-weak-multidiagrams-admit-coherent-all-index-regular-polygon-data]], [[thm-globally-weak-zero-marked-polygons-have-finite-counts-and-a-infinity-boundaries]])

Its proof first obtains the finite lower-index band before taking limits, and retains all actual Spin-c extension and marked-degree data. ([[thm-strictly-admissible-triple-free-polygons-have-full-marked-low-dimensional-counts]])

facts.label: F5

The central component is not divided by translation; its autonomous escaping end levels are. ([[thm-fixed-background-zero-marked-continuation-counts-give-chain-homotopy-equivalences]])

facts.label: F6

Actual finite-ended polygon charts, source-local universal regularity, domain-energy bounds, stable-source compactness and regular-tree gluing are proved without global or strong admissibility as premises; those assumptions enter only their applications to energy bounds. The bounded-energy autonomous argument uses dense time-slice injective sites and its free-image test. facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Full-module admissibility tests EVERY intended Spin-c sector, even an empty-generator one. The finite Heegaard Spin construction supplies a determinant-trivial sector, so this is equivalent to the global mixed-sign condition. Every supplied complete geometric diagram has the actual finite winding preparation to a globally weak one. Actual globally weak chosen hat complexes and their square-zero finite differentials exist. ([[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]], [[lem-complete-heegaard-data-have-a-zero-chern-spin-c-sector]], [[thm-globally-weak-closed-heegaard-data-admit-a-finite-chosen-hat-complex]], [[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The actual circular top cycles, top-triangle products and quadrilateral counts give handleslide chain maps with the displayed explicit inverse homotopies. Actual attaching isotopies have regular-interval transport and birth/death equivalences. Their proof supplies the uniform paired-dual winding preparation and explicit unit-pair cancellation. ([[thm-globally-weak-hat-handleslides-have-explicit-inverse-homotopies]], [[thm-globally-weak-hat-attaching-isotopies-have-actual-inverse-maps]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Ordinary stabilization in a disk in the basepoint region has literal inverse chain isomorphisms $x\mapsto x\times c$ and $x\times c\mapsto x$, with zero inverse homotopies. Its separator proof is applied only in that region. ([[thm-hat-heegaard-stabilization-has-explicit-inverse-chain-maps]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Transported diagram data identify actual counts by inverse chain isomorphisms. Actual fixed-background continuation now allows independently supplied generator jets and full boundary tensors. After that operation aligns chosen canonical data, the stated fixed-background full-boundary and changing-background theorems give actual equivalences with their common generator prescriptions. ([[lem-closed-pointed-diagram-isomorphisms-identify-hat-counts]], [[thm-fixed-symmetric-background-hat-complexes-with-different-boundary-values-are-equivalent]], [[thm-changing-complex-background-zero-marked-continuations-are-chain-equivalences]], [[thm-fixed-background-hat-continuations-allow-independent-generator-data]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Any two supplied complete pointed splittings of this Y are joined by the actual finite general-manifold based geometric move theorem. It makes no assertion that its intermediate diagrams are admissible. ([[thm-based-heegaard-moves-generate-closed-three-manifold-diagram-equivalence]])

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Broad auxiliary disks have same-boundary neat preparations and smooth standard cut balls. The finite graph model embeds an abstract handlebody in $S^3$ for this preparation. Smooth Schoenflies there supplies actual smooth balls. Marked planar cap transfers are actual disk slides, and two rooted-tree reductions of one extended ball cut are connected by actual marked slides. ([[lem-proper-compression-disks-admit-neat-witnesses-with-standard-cut-balls]], [[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]], [[lem-marked-planar-cut-surface-regions-are-realized-by-disk-slides]], [[lem-empty-cut-ball-births-erase-to-balanced-disk-slides]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] In the actual flat torus coordinates the meridians $\alpha=(1,0)$ and $\beta=(1,3\varepsilon)$, $\varepsilon=\pm1$, have exactly three intersections, no nonzero normalized periodic domain, no relative disk between different generators, and only the constant relative class at an equal generator. Its proof is the explicit compact-disk lift and affine contraction in the plane, independently of a holomorphic equation. ([[lem-straight-three-intersection-torus-diagram-has-no-nonconstant-disks]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The actual allowed hat data have nonnegative region degrees and energy bounded by a fixed positive linear combination of those degrees. Relative homotopies preserve these degrees, since their boundary stays on the attaching circles, away from each region test point. ([[lem-nearly-symmetric-polygons-have-positive-domains-and-degree-energy-bounds]], [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The full hat complex and the proved actual move maps identify its homology with the full closed-manifold invariant. The filling convention identifies the unknot-exterior meridian with its preferred longitude $\lambda_U$, and the attached meridian for $L(3,1)$ with $\lambda_U+3\mu_U$. ([[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]], [[thm-hat-heegaard-floer-is-a-closed-three-manifold-invariant]], [[def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The general $Y$ vertex modules and increasing filtration are the ones explicitly specified in the Statement. The branched-cover module is their later special application, rather than a premise restricting this general surgery statement to $S^3$.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The actual analytic foundations [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]] supply finite zero-basepoint disk and polygon counts, compact one-dimensional boundaries, exhaustive gluing and the resulting identities on the stated operation-specific admissible data: global weak data for all-sector sums, or the prescribed ordinary weak or strict specified-Spin-c families. Positive-rank triples use explicit small triple-free representatives with transported labels; rank zero uses the point model. This supplies neither a subordinate surgery multidiagram nor a calculation that its distinguished top inputs are cycles or satisfy the required higher sums. It does not identify surgery total homology with a filling.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The total homology is interpreted as an invariant of the filled manifold only after closed-manifold Heegaard Floer invariance ([[thm-hat-heegaard-floer-is-a-closed-three-manifold-invariant]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **External input — actual surgery data and top sums.** Ozsváth–Szabó, *On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers*, arXiv:math/0309170v1, §4.2, pp.21–23, equation(10) and Lemma4.5: for an ordered framed link in an arbitrary closed oriented three-manifold, the bouquet-subordinate attaching systems use meridians $\beta_i$, framing curves $\gamma_i$, and meridian-added curves $\delta_i$, with separately labelled Hamiltonian copies for unchanged systems. On the compatible admissible surgery data the distinguished top inputs are cycles and all monotone top-input sums $M_{AB}$ below vanish. This is the imported operation-specific construction/calculation, not a consequence newly deduced from [F2]. Only its mod-two version is used.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] **External input — actual single-coordinate surgery cone.** The same source, Theorem4.7 and its proof, pp.24–27, equation(12), supplies a quasi-isomorphism between the cone of the $0\to1$ two-handle triangle map and the third, meridian filling. Its quadrilateral/top-generator calculation and the cyclic Hamiltonian-copy construction are included in this import; no merely formal null-composition is substituted for that calculation. Its hypotheses are the surgery triad with the subordinate admissible choices above, not an arbitrary pair of chain maps.

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] **External input — total-cube filling comparison.** The proof of Theorem4.1, p.27, supplies acyclicity of the enlarged three-valued coordinate complex with its ACTUAL higher polygon entries. It yields the homology comparison with one coordinate filled by $\infty$, and induction gives the all-$\infty$ filling. Theorem4.1 and Remark4.2, p.17, identify the first differential as the sum of immediate two-handle maps and allow flattening by $|I|$. This imports the actual total construction; it does not assert guessed canonical coherent comparison maps between arbitrary presentations.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The double branched cover and its orientation are defined and well-defined up to oriented diffeomorphism ([[lem-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link-well-defined]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The group is defined by the closed-manifold disk-count complex ([[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The actual analytic foundations [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]] provide finite zero-basepoint disk and polygon counts, compactified boundaries, exhaustive gluing and the resulting identities under their actual operation-specific global weak, ordinary specified-sector weak or strict admissibility hypotheses. They include positive-rank pointed triple-free representatives and the rank-zero point target. These local identities do not compute the exterior-algebra basis or its $H_1$ action, prove a named top input is a cycle, or identify an unlink saddle map with a prescribed Frobenius map.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **External input — actual unlink Floer module and handle maps.** Ozsváth–Szabó, arXiv:math/0309170v1, Proposition6.1 and proof, pp.32–33: over $\mathbb F_2$, $\widehat{HF}(\#^r(S^2\times S^1))$ is a free rank-one module over $\Lambda^*H_1$, generated by a class $\Theta$. A zero-framed two-handle killing a summand generator induces the exterior quotient, and its dual split operation induces wedge with the new kernel generator. The statement includes the actual triangle-map/$H_1$-action computation, not merely the dimension of the group.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] **External input — simultaneously compatible state bases.** The same source, Proposition6.2, pp.33–34, including all four cases and Figure11, identifies a based unlink state with this module using lifts $\gamma_i$ of arcs from the marked circle $S_0$ to each other circle $S_i$, with $[\gamma_0]=0$. Its commutative square(13) identifies EVERY immediate surgery edge in the same state bases. Unmarked merge identifies $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$; unmarked split has new kernel $\gamma_1-\gamma_2$; setting $\gamma_0=0$ gives both marked cases. This is an external input at the chosen finite diagram, not arbitrary unlink naturality or a new locally proved count.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] [[lem-spin-c-lifts-exist-iff-w2-has-an-integral-lift]] proves, by actual Spin transition functions and finite-partition cocycles, that an integral lift of $w_2(TB)$ gives a Spin$^c$ lift of the tangent frame bundle. facts.text: [F2] For a compact oriented four-manifold with boundary, cap product gives $H^j(B,Y;\mathbb Z)\cong H_{4-j}(B;\mathbb Z)$ and $H^j(B;\mathbb Z)\cong H_{4-j}(B,Y;\mathbb Z)$ under AC ([[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Cup product is natural under inclusion; for a rational homology sphere, Poincare duality identifies $H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, and the surgery supplier fixes the chain-linking convention as $-A^{-1}$ for a nonsingular matrix $A$ ([[prop-cup-product-is-natural-unital-and-associative]], [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], [[lem-cyclic-cover-linking-form-inverse-matrix]]).

facts.text: [F6] Once a Spin$^c$ lift is given, the isomorphism classes of lifts form an affine $H^2(-;\mathbb Z)$-space ([[lem-spin-c-structures-form-an-h2-torsor]]). Boundary restriction is the actual normal-first rank-four-to-rank-three principal reduction and is equivariant for the restriction of line bundles and $H^2$ ([[lem-boundary-spin-c-restriction-and-line-twists-are-equivariant]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] Every compact connected oriented smooth rational homology four-ball admits at least one Spin$^c$ structure ([[lem-rational-homology-four-ball-admits-spinc]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] AC is assumed by the UCT, tubular-neighbourhood, Thom, Poincare-duality, geometric-intersection, and self-intersection suppliers; AC implies the ACω hypotheses of the lens-space convention ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The standard filtration $\mathbb{CP}^0\subset\mathbb{CP}^1\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ and affine charts give one cell in dimensions $0,2,4$; cellular and universal-coefficient comparison compute its integral homology and cohomology ([[def-complex-projective-space-and-holomorphic-charts]], [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]], [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Excision identifies $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^2,B_2;\mathbb Z)$ with $H^*(N(Q),\partial N(Q);\mathbb Z)$, and the normalized oriented rank-two Thom class identifies the latter with $H^{*-2}(Q;\mathbb Z)$ and evaluates $+1$ on each positive normal disk. Its relative-to-absolute image in degree two is the Poincare dual of $Q$, with sign $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=+1$ ([[thm-excision-for-singular-cohomology]], [[thm-thom-isomorphism-for-oriented-vector-bundles]], [[def-thom-class-by-fiberwise-normalization]], [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The complex orientation supplies the fundamental class; Poincare duality identifies $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^2;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_2(\mathbb{CP}^2;\mathbb Z)$; the geometric intersection pairing equals the Poincare-dual cup pairing and depends only on homology classes; homotopic maps induce the same homology map; and the local sign of a transverse intersection is determined by the ordered tangent orientations ([[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]], [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], [[thm-geometric-intersection-equals-the-poincare-dual-cup-pairing]], [[cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology]], [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]], [[def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold]], [[def-oriented-intersection-number]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The self-intersection of a compact oriented surface in an oriented four-manifold equals the Euler number of its oriented normal bundle ([[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]], [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The lens-space convention defines $L(p,1)$ by $+p$ filling of the standard unknot exterior; the nonsingular surgery matrix gives $H_1\cong\mathbb Z/p$ ([[def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention]], [[lem-cyclic-cover-linking-form-inverse-matrix]]). The lens-space convention assumes countable choice, which follows from AC ([[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] The cohomology long exact sequence of the pair $(\mathbb{CP}^2,B_2)$ computes the cohomology of the complement from the relative and absolute groups ([[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-cohomology]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Admissible vectors have embedded normal realizations by [[lem-normal-coordinate-matching-equations-and-finite-bounds]], steps 1.1–1.2. This is the finite placement of compatible disk copies and ordered face-side gluings, not an existence theorem about essential disks.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[lem-triangular-normal-arcs-admit-braid-position-stable-under-partial-regular-switches]] constructs each face from three monotone strips and one central normal chord per arc. Every partial regular reconnection consists of embedded normal arcs of unchanged type counts, and no remaining crossing is a self-crossing of an arc. Its local regular choice is characterized uniquely by preservation of the two normal arc types, including after a partial reconnection.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[lem-compatible-normal-disk-boundary-paths-have-a-unique-type-preserving-switch]] gives exactly one pairing of two normal disk boundary paths, cut at distinct common faces, which preserves their two original disk types. The five cases in that proof are entirely in the original tetrahedron.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The cap placement and circle elimination in [[lem-compatible-normal-surfaces-admit-finite-circle-free-tetrahedral-position]], steps 2.1–7.1, require the face-arc systems to be embedded within each family, transverse between families, and to have at most one crossing per pair. They use straightness only to establish that last property in step 4.1. Thus the very same cap and replacement construction applies to the face-braid systems of [F2], which have all three properties. It preserves the vectors, the abstract disk-side gluing data and the boundary homotopies.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Every original tetrahedral double arc joins distinct faces, and every global double curve therefore meets some face. The regular switch at any crossed face is the monotone through reconnection in one of its three strips. Its opposite pairs the two outer-side branches and the two gate-side branches. Prior regular switches retain this same monotone strip description. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]], [[lem-triangular-normal-arcs-admit-braid-position-stable-under-partial-regular-switches]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The replacement proof in [[lem-essential-pl-disks-admit-normal-replacements]] uses tetrahedral cap replacements and compressions that fix the face boundary curves and edge intersections; sphere discards can only remove such intersections. Once all tetrahedral pieces are disks, an edge-return produces an actual edge bigon and removes two edge intersections, retaining an essential disk in the boundary-edge case. All later moves are nonincreasing in edge weight. These are the explicit local moves of that supplier’s proof, not an isotopy or irreducibility claim.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The projective plane is the finite polygonal surface with attaching word $aa$ and is nonorientable. Removing a point in the open polygonal face gives an open Mobius band, which retracts onto its core circle; this retraction is obtained by its rectangle-with-reversed-ends model. Thus every polygonal loop may be moved off that point and then onto a power of the core, while twice the core bounds the polygonal face. ([[ex-projective-plane-polygonal-schema]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Two parametrized finite PL three-balls glued along marked parametrized boundary disks by a given PL map form a parametrized PL three-ball. Consequently a finite tree of such pieces is a parametrized ball, by successively deleting a leaf and applying that assertion to its one attaching window. Prisms with convex disk bases are themselves parametrized balls. ([[lem-parametrized-pl-balls-absorb-standard-boundary-windows]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] No closed nonorientable PL surface embeds in the standard PL three-sphere, and therefore none embeds in a parametrized PL three-ball: compose its parameter with the standard inclusion of the convex ball into $\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$. ([[lem-no-closed-nonorientable-pl-surface-in-s-three]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Compatible admissible vectors have regular diagrams in which all partial regular resolutions retain the normal tetrahedral disk pieces. The vector determines the abstract surface and the homotopy classes of corresponding boundary curves. These properties persist when some components are absorbed by performing all their regular switches with the other family: only the remaining old double curves are left. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A connected finite surface has Euler characteristic at most two. With boundary it has Euler characteristic at most one; if positive it is a disk. A closed surface of Euler characteristic two is a sphere, and a boundary surface of Euler characteristic zero is an annulus or a Mobius band, distinguished by respectively two or one boundary circles. ([[lem-positive-euler-finite-pl-surfaces-are-disks-spheres-or-projective-planes]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Euler characteristic is additive under regular sums. For a proper double arc, cutting raises the total by two and its two joining strips lower it by two; for a double circle the change is zero. The finite strip cell count proves this also for partial immersed normalizations.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The normal vector determines the abstract surface and the boundary homotopy class of its corresponding curves. Actual regular diagrams retain their original normal tetrahedral disk pieces and their rectangular exchange neighborhoods; exchange strips miss the original edges. [[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] An embedded essential PL disk has an essential normal replacement componentwise nonincreasing on the original edges. The finite cap preparations and compressions used for that replacement do not assert preservation of its ambient isotopy class. [[lem-essential-pl-disks-admit-normal-replacements]]

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] If two admissible normal vectors have original-edge counts averaging to those of $D$, their normal vectors average to $d$. If both are least-weight essential disks, the lexicographic choice forces both vectors to be $d$. [[lem-admissible-normal-vectors-have-rigid-edge-count-averages]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A disk patch cut out by actual exchange traces, with no original-boundary side and with its trace segments joining distinct original normal-cell sides, has positive original-edge weight. [[lem-normal-exchange-disk-patches-have-positive-edge-weight]]

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable choice is the standing hypothesis; the local finite rounding, surface normal forms and smooth isotopy interfaces below use this hypothesis. ([[def-countable-choice]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Every essential exterior disk has longitude class up to sign and odd intersection with the original fibre meridian. ([[lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A peripheral curve of core degree $1$ or $-1$ cobounds a finite piecewise smooth annulus with the core, smooth on a collar of the core boundary. ([[lem-degree-one-peripheral-curves-cobound-annuli-with-tube-core]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A finite compatible whole-star surface with an already smooth boundary collar has a smooth embedded replacement with the same topology and exactly the same boundary, fixed on a smaller collar. Smooth transverse proper disks conversely have PL proper approximations preserving the boundary's isotopy class. ([[lem-finite-compatible-pl-surfaces-admit-relative-smooth-roundings]], [[lem-smooth-proper-disks-have-compatible-pl-approximations]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A smooth knot bounds a smooth embedded disk exactly when it has genus zero, and genus zero is equivalent under countable choice to smooth ambient isotopy to the oriented unknot. ([[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The PL convention here is the compatible PL structure of the supplied smooth exterior, represented by a whole-star smooth triangulation with boundary subcomplex and tangent-half-space fans. A PL disk can therefore be made a subcomplex by finite common subdivision, and its simplex restrictions have injective derivative fans. This is the ordinary meaning of PL in this smooth exterior, rather than a separate arbitrary topological marking. A representing finite whole-star triangulation is obtained by the finite coordinate-box and fitting construction of [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]; that supplier explicitly declares its ambient full-AC hypothesis dispensable and its actual finite construction uses no additional choice. The rounding and approximation clauses of [F3] use this same chosen compatible structure throughout.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] In the reduced pair, every nonempty partial selection of remaining regular switches has connected normalization; no circle separates both summands. Their edge weights add to $w(F)$. All remaining tetrahedral traces join distinct faces and the regular pairings extend consistently along whole double curves. ([[lem-regular-normal-sum-diagrams-have-reduced-connected-pairs]], [[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The finite graph-neighborhood construction in [[lem-positive-euler-finite-pl-surfaces-are-disks-spheres-or-projective-planes]] gives a connected boundary surface with Euler characteristic $-1$ as a disk with two rectangular bands. If it has three boundary circles, both bands must increase the boundary count by one, since each changes it by at most one. Each such attachment joins two intervals on the same circle without a twist, splits that circle into two, and removes one disk from a planar model. Thus this surface is a pair of pants. This is a finite band calculation, not an invocation of full surface classification or choice.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A simple PL circle on a PL sphere bounds two disks. A circle inside a pair of pants is either inessential or parallel to a boundary circle: cap the three boundary circles on a sphere, and choose a side of the given circle containing at most one cap. With zero caps it is a disk, and with one it is an annulus after removing the cap. These are finite polygonal separation and triangulation constructions. ([[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]], [[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] An irregular partial resolution containing an embedded essential disk as a parametrizing component yields an essential normal disk of weight strictly below the diagram's total original weight. ([[lem-irregular-switches-in-original-face-braids-give-strict-essential-disk-improvement]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Every remaining regular pairing continues consistently around its double curve. No remaining circle separates both summands. Every nonempty partial regular resolution has connected normalization, and the weights of the two summands add to $w(F)$. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]], [[lem-regular-normal-sum-diagrams-have-reduced-connected-pairs]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A connected finite triangulated surface with boundary and Euler characteristic $1$ is a disk. If instead its Euler characteristic is zero, it is an annulus with two boundary circles or a Mobius band with one. The finite proofs add no choice assumption. ([[lem-connected-normal-surface-chi-one-is-disk]], [[lem-positive-euler-finite-pl-surfaces-are-disks-spheres-or-projective-planes]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A projective plane has Euler characteristic $1$, as is seen from its finite one-vertex, one-edge, one-face model. ([[ex-projective-plane-polygonal-schema]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A small intrinsic neighborhood of a simple circle in a finite PL surface is an annulus or a Mobius band, obtained by following its finite rectangular arc charts around the circle. The two possibilities are distinguished by whether its transverse interval returns without reversal or with reversal. Removing either neighborhood preserves Euler characteristic, since both and their attaching boundary circles have Euler characteristic zero.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Every preliminary regular resolution retains embedded normal tetrahedral disk pieces and, in each face, embedded parametrizing arcs consisting of one central chord and two distinct monotone outer strips. All remaining crossings occur in those strips; their regular reconnection is outer-to-gate, and the irregular one joins the two outer branches and the two gate branches. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]], [[lem-triangular-normal-arcs-admit-braid-position-stable-under-partial-regular-switches]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Essential PL disks admit finite normal replacements componentwise nonincreasing on the original edges. The preparation fixes face curves until the tetrahedral pieces are disks, except for discarding components; an embedded face arc returning to the same edge then supplies a bigon removing two edge intersections while retaining an essential disk. ([[lem-essential-pl-disks-admit-normal-replacements]], [[lem-irregular-switches-in-original-face-braids-give-strict-essential-disk-improvement]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The two reduced summands are connected embedded normal surfaces with positive weights adding to $w(F)$. Their regular full resolution is a disk with essential boundary, and every nonempty partial regular resolution has connected normalization. No remaining intersection curve or proper arc separates both summands. The retained local double arcs join distinct tetrahedral faces and therefore distinct sides of each normal disk. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]], [[lem-regular-normal-sum-diagrams-have-reduced-connected-pairs]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] A connected finite PL surface with positive Euler characteristic is a disk, sphere or projective plane. A connected boundary surface with Euler characteristic zero is an annulus or a Mobius band; with Euler characteristic one it is a disk. A disjoint properly embedded arc family in a disk cuts it into disks. ([[lem-positive-euler-finite-pl-surfaces-are-disks-spheres-or-projective-planes]], [[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]], [[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Neither reduced summand here is a sphere or projective plane. These exclusions use the retained original diagram and least edge weight, without ambient restrictions. ([[lem-reduced-original-normal-pairs-for-a-least-weight-essential-disk-have-no-spherical-summand]], [[lem-reduced-original-normal-pairs-for-a-least-weight-essential-disk-have-no-projective-plane-summand]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A boundary disk patch satisfying the trace condition in [F1] has positive weight. Normal replacement of an essential proper PL disk gives an essential normal disk with no larger edge weight. ([[lem-normal-exchange-disk-patches-have-positive-edge-weight]], [[lem-essential-pl-disks-admit-normal-replacements]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] If a resolution of the retained diagram includes an irregular switch and has a parametrizing component whose image is an embedded essential proper disk, there is an essential normal disk of weight strictly below $w(P)+w(H)$. ([[lem-irregular-switches-in-original-face-braids-give-strict-essential-disk-improvement]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Switch every other original curve regularly and leave the selected curve unswitched. This partial diagram has embedded normal tetrahedral parametrizing disks and only that one remaining double curve. Full regular resolution recovers $F$. All changes miss the original edges. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] If a closed union of parametrizing components of a retained diagram has edge weight $W$, an irregular resolution producing an embedded proper essential disk gives an essential normal disk of weight less than $W$, even when that retained union is one immersed component. ([[lem-closed-normal-subdiagrams-inherit-strict-irregular-disk-improvement]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A fundamental admissible vector has no decomposition into two nonzero admissible integer vectors. Every nonempty embedded normal component has a nonzero such vector. ([[def-normal-surface-coordinate-box]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] Any partial regular resolution has embedded normal tetrahedral parametrizing disks and only its unswitched double curves. Its total vector and edge counts are unchanged. [[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]]

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Restricting to whole parametrizing components closed under their remaining double curves retains the original face strands and switches. In a face strip containing an irregular switch, the first such switch from the original edge joins two outer strands and produces a parametrizing arc returning to that edge. This is the actual local construction in steps 1.2–2.1 of [[lem-irregular-switches-in-original-face-braids-give-strict-essential-disk-improvement]], and its restriction is verified in steps 1.1–2.1 of [[lem-closed-normal-subdiagrams-inherit-strict-irregular-disk-improvement]]. The return arc exists before any hypothesis about which component contains its endpoints.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] For an embedded essential PL disk containing such an embedded face-return arc, the normal-replacement procedure either already loses an edge point in its preliminary moves, or preserves its face curve until tetrahedral pieces are disks and then removes two edge intersections at the return. It therefore gives strict decrease relative to this disk's own weight. For a second essential PL disk, the procedure is nonincreasing. These are the actual finite moves of [[lem-essential-pl-disks-admit-normal-replacements]] and proof step 4.1 of [[lem-irregular-switches-in-original-face-braids-give-strict-essential-disk-improvement]], not an inference that the old one-output bound applies to each component separately.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A disk cap cut off by one proper trace on a normal disk has positive edge weight, by the distinct-side cell count. [[lem-normal-exchange-disk-patches-have-positive-edge-weight]]

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The explicit normal-replacement moves do not increase the count at any individual original edge: tetrahedral cap changes and compressions fix edge points, sphere discards remove points, and an edge bigon removes two points on that edge without adding points on another. Thus an essential PL disk $D$ has an essential normal replacement $U$ with $N_e(U)\le N_e(D)$ for every $e$. ([[lem-essential-pl-disks-admit-normal-replacements]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] If two admissible normal vectors have edge-count sum $2N(F)$, their vector sum is $2v(F)$. If they are also least-weight essential disks, lexicographic minimality of $v(F)$ makes both equal $v(F)$. ([[lem-admissible-normal-vectors-have-rigid-edge-count-averages]])

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The caps are disjoint and adjacent. Undoing this exchange while all others remain regular leaves one connected affected parametrizing normalization, with only its one remaining self-double curve and with edge weight $w(D)$. A disconnected one would split $v(D)$ into two embedded nonempty normal vectors, contrary to fundamentalness. ([[lem-same-copy-exchanges-on-least-fundamental-disks-have-disjoint-adjacent-caps]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] An irregular resolution of that closed affected subdiagram, if it has an embedded proper essential disk output, gives a normal essential disk of weight less than $w(D)$. ([[lem-closed-normal-subdiagrams-inherit-strict-irregular-disk-improvement]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Each of these caps is a disk patch for the two selected trace components alone. Its trace arcs in normal tetrahedral disks join distinct sides. A disk patch with zero or one original-boundary arc has positive edge weight. ([[lem-normal-exchange-disk-patches-have-positive-edge-weight]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] An embedded essential PL disk has a normal essential replacement componentwise nonincreasing on every original edge. If two admissible normal vectors have edge counts averaging to those of $D$, their normal vectors average to $v(D)$; lexicographic minimality among eligible disks then forces both to equal $v(D)$. facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] There are at least two original leaf disk patches of $P$, each of positive edge weight. The partner $H$ is an annulus or Mobius band; every original intersection arc is nonseparating in $H$, and cutting all the arcs decomposes both summands into disks. facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For the chosen leaf, the opposite end disk satisfies $N(E')=N(E)$ at every original edge, and therefore $w(E')=w(E)$. ([[lem-boundary-exchange-leaf-caps-for-a-least-weight-disk-have-rigid-edge-counts]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] In the full resolution, the two traces of each switched proper arc can be retained on the resulting normal disk as disjoint proper arcs. The exchange rectangle between them has interior off $F$. Cutting $F$ at those traces leaves the original cut patches with small half-switch-band collars attached to their trace sides. These collars lie in the switching neighborhoods, miss $T^{(1)}$, and change neither the patch topology nor its number of trace sides. Each trace segment in a normal cell joins distinct original tetrahedral faces, since it is parallel to the corresponding original double arc. The construction and its regular disk switch preserve this face incidence. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A finite proper arc family cuts a disk into disks with a tree as adjacency graph. A zero-edge disk corridor with two trace sides and two original-boundary sides has a finite product parametrization within its original normal cells. ([[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]], [[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]], [[lem-zero-edge-normal-exchange-rectangles-and-annuli-have-cellwise-product-structures]])

facts.text: [F1] A minimum original leaf $E\subset P$ has positive weight $m$. Its opposite cap $B=E'$ has the same edge counts and weight, is disjoint from $E$, and contains exactly one minimum original leaf $L\subset P$. Either it equals $L$ or it differs from $L$ by a zero-edge rectangular corridor. facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Each exchange arc has a small rectangular exchange surface between its two full-resolution traces. Its interior misses $F$, its end intervals lie in the original boundary faces, and the rectangles for different arcs are disjoint. Cutting the two traces restores the four original rays. The original unswitched continuation pairs opposite rays, while the two uncrossings pair adjacent rays. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]])

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] Resolving any subset of original double arcs regularly leaves, in every tetrahedron, embedded normal triangle or quadrilateral disks, possibly forming an immersed global normalization along the remaining unswitched arcs. Every nonempty normalization component therefore meets the original one-skeleton: any one of its tetrahedral disks has normal vertices on that one-skeleton. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]])

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The retained trace arcs on $F$ are disjoint proper arcs. Two disk caps cut off by two such arcs are either disjoint, nested, or have union $F$. This follows by cutting the disk along the two arcs into three disks in a path and considering which side of each arc is the chosen cap. ([[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]], [[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]])

facts.text: [F1] A disjoint finite arrangement of proper PL disks in a parametrized PL ball cuts it into parametrized balls. Corresponding boundary-circle and disk maps extend over the cut balls and paste to a PL homeomorphism. The proof cuts along one disk, caps it on the two boundary sides, and uses finite PL Schoenflies, then iterates. ([[lem-equal-normal-vectors-have-ambient-cell-homeomorphisms-and-disk-copy-products]])

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Disjoint proper polygonal arcs cut a polygonal disk into parametrized polygonal disks. An endpoint-order-preserving correspondence of the boundary and the arcs extends over these regions: choose the interval maps on the arcs, then cone compatible boundary triangulations of each region. ([[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]], [[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]])

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The end disks, tetrahedral prisms, face strips and original edge intervals are the actual supplied product cells, not an unmarked topological identification. A component of $A$ in a face strip is a proper arc between its two horizontal boundary arcs. Its endpoints miss the edge intervals, because $A$ misses the one-skeleton. The corresponding rectangles and face arcs are finite, disjoint and embedded by hypothesis.

facts.label: F3

Its only alternatives are sphere plus annulus, or two disks. facts.label: F5

All partial regular resolutions have genuine normal tetrahedral disk pieces, and hence every nonempty normalization component has positive weight. The trace arcs are disjoint, proper, and join distinct sides in each normal cell. facts.text: [F2] A connected reduced alternating diagram realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link, under countable choice, which follows here from full AC ([[thm-reduced-alternating-diagram-minimizes-crossings]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] **Imported external prime theorem.** For reduced prime oriented alternating link diagrams and a given orientation-preserving homeomorphism of their represented oriented link pairs, the Menasco–Thistlethwaite Main Theorem gives a finite composite of flypes inducing that given map's oriented component correspondence. We use the diagram sequence with sphere planar isotopies allowed. This is the published Main Theorem on printed p. 116 of *The classification of alternating links* (1993), not a locally reconstructed proof of its prime case. Its elementary crossing-centered flypes have the turnover convention of [[def-flype-crossing-ball-and-alternating-tangle-data]]; choosing projection charts gives the sphere planar isotopies of the statement.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **Imported external primeness theorem.** A connected reduced alternating projection with no simple circle meeting it transversely in two ordinary points and having crossings on both sides represents a prime link, provided the represented link is nontrivial. This is the diagrammatic primeness consequence of Menasco, *Closed incompressible surfaces in alternating knot and link complements* (1984), Theorem 1(b), printed p. 37, with proof on pp. 41–42. The theorem applies to links, not only knots. It is imported here rather than reconstructed from the other normal-form research.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] Given two finite decomposition-sphere systems of the same nonsplit oriented link with nontrivial prime capped factors and their reduced alternating factor diagrams, the component-marked comparison and lift applies. Its actual factor correspondences retain the oriented global component names, cap parameters, roots and boundary collars. Supplying the prime flype sequences with those induced component maps yields the original diagram sequence; no puncture-relative prime theorem is required ([[lem-component-marked-prime-decomposition-comparisons-lift-prime-flype-sequences]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text: [F6] Reducedness, alternatingness, sphere planar isotopy and flypes have the stated diagram meanings ([[def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram]], [[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]], [[def-flype-crossing-ball-and-alternating-tangle-data]]).
